#5262. Akash’s Solana Migration Clears November 2 Vote at 97%, With Four More On-Chain Decisions Ahead

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

AKT stakers are close to approving Akash's move from Cosmos to Solana, with Mintscan projecting a pass at 97.2% yes as voting enters its final hours.

But a yes on Proposal 346 opens a door rather than completing a move. Before a single AKT reaches Solana, two independent audits and at least two more on-chain votes still have to happen.

The summary going around is simple: Akash is leaving Cosmos for Solana. The proposal itself is narrower than that, and the details matter for anyone holding AKT.

Proposal 346 on akashnet-2, titled "Migrate the Akash Protocol to Solana," closes at 15:02 UTC on November 2. A yes vote approves the migration plan and authorises AKT to launch as an SPL token through a one-way portal that stays open for two years. It does not set a cutover date, it does not move a single lease, and on its own it does not open the portal.

The technical spec for that portal was published the day after voting opened. It shows how many further steps lie between this vote and a working SPL AKT.

The proposal text in Akash's AEP repository says a yes vote does two things:

It also says plainly what it doesn't do: "it does not set a cutover date and does not move the marketplace." Live leases, staking and governance on akashnet-2 continue as normal. The marketplace moves only after audits and rehearsals pass and "a separate cutover proposal passes on this chain."

A no vote would stop the whole plan. In the proposal's words: "Nothing moves; the token does not launch and the program returns to option analysis."

At 08:43 UTC on November 2, about six hours before voting closed, Mintscan's page for Proposal 346 showed an expected result of "Will PASS":

Turnout stood at 68.80% of bonded stake, against a quorum of 33.40%. The same figures can be read from Akash's own chain API, through the proposal object and its tally endpoint.

Mintscan's 97.2% is yes as a share of all votes cast. Akash's pass threshold leaves abstentions out, and on that basis yes stands at about 98.7%, far above the 50% needed. The veto share is negligible.

The tally has barely changed since early morning. A read of the chain at 07:29 UTC showed almost exactly the same totals, with only a handful of AKT added to the yes side. With turnout and margin that large, the outcome is not in doubt. The more useful question is what happens after it passes.

The portal's design is in AEP-95, "One-Way AKT Sink to Solana,", a draft published on October 27 by core developers Artur Troian and Joseph Chalabi. It describes a "deliberately one-way" bridge with no return path. The authors say this removes "the largest class of bridge attacks."

Why supply doesn't change: every SPL AKT is backed by AKT locked on Akash, and nothing is minted independently on Solana. The token is a legacy SPL mint with six decimals and no freeze authority.

The spec's own risk table names the biggest trust point. The upgrade authority over the Solana programs could "mint without limit." That power is meant to sit with a time-locked multisig appointed by Akash governance, with monitors set to alert on every admin action.

At launch, SPL AKT has no protocol role. It will support "transfers and DEX liquidity only, with no staking or governance rights." Inflation stays on Akash. To seed trading, Overclock Labs, Akash's core developer, will send 1 million AKT through the bridge to a Solana treasury vault. That deposit follows the same rules as everyone else's.

Proposal 346 requires "two independent audits of the token and portal code before launch," with reports published within 30 days. AEP-95's launch sequence shows what that requirement means on-chain.

So Proposal 346 is the first of at least five on-chain decisions. The "2 to 3 weeks" launch estimate depends on the audits finishing and the upgrade and parameter votes passing on schedule.

For now, nothing. The proposal's disclosures set out what changes later:

Discussion of the proposal continues in GitHub Discussion #1123.

The proposal lists four items as "still open, to be settled and published before the cutover proposal":

The second item matters most to holders. The portal closes two years after launch, and the proposal doesn't yet say what happens to AKT that hasn't crossed by then. The final tally will confirm whether the plan goes ahead, but that answer, and the decisions in the votes that follow, will matter more to most holders than today's margin.

The Dogecoin community gets a security alert after wallet provider Trezor revealed a suspected hardware implant in its Safe 5 device bought from CryptoBilis.

Dogecoin community member Mishaboar urged users who purchased a Trezor device from CryptoBilis in March this year or later to take immediate precautions, including moving their funds to a completely new wallet with a freshly generated recovery seed.

"If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible," Mishaboar wrote.

If you bought a Trezor from CryptoBilis in March 2026 or later, move your funds to a completely new wallet, with a newly generated recovery seed, as soon as possible. Use a device and wallet you trust to create the new wallet. If your wallet supports an additional passphrase, use it (and remember to write it down in your offline backups). NEVER reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does NOT make your funds safe. An ELI5: I know this is obvious to many of you, but in my experience some people don't realize that hardware wallets don't actually "contain" their coins. Your coins "live" on the blockchain. Your wallet only holds the keys that allow you to access and spend them. If someone else has a copy of those keys, they can access your funds from anywhere in the world, from any device where those keys are imported. They don't need your physical little device or your phone to access it.

Users are warned never to reuse a recovery seed from a wallet that might have been compromised. Simply resetting the device or importing the same seed into another wallet does not make funds safe either.

Mishaboar highlighted a critical security principle that may not seem obvious to all users: hardware wallets do not actually "contain" coins—the coins "live" on the blockchain. The wallet only holds the keys that allow access to and spending of the coins. If someone obtains these keys, they can access the funds from anywhere in the world on any device where the keys are imported, without needing the physical device or the user's phone.

Mishaboar's warning follows a recent update from Trezor regarding CryptoBilis, in which the company disclosed that it had been alerted through responsible disclosure to a suspected hardware implant in a Trezor Safe 5 device purchased from CryptoBilis in August 2026.

According to Trezor, the reported device has not yet been received for physical examination. However, the company said it considers the report credible enough to notify customers while its security team investigates. No CryptoBilis buyer has reported losing funds to the company so far.

In light of this, affected users are urged to move their funds to a newly created wallet with a new seed as soon as possible. Those who have not yet set up their device should never do so using an existing wallet backup (recovery phrase), nor share this information with anyone.

It's the 18th anniversary of the Bitcoin whitepaper. Today marks the historic date on which its pseudonymous creator Satoshi Nakamoto published the blueprint for the first digital cash.

On Oct. 31, 2008, a nine-page white paper called "Bitcoin: A Peer-to-Peer Electronic Cash System" was published, laying out a radical vision for transferring value electronically without the need for conventional financial intermediaries.

Bitcoin supporters, exchanges, and the rest of the crypto community are filling social media platform X with celebratory wishes on the 18th anniversary of Bitcoin's unveiling to the world.

Bitcoin proponent and Strategy Chairman Michael Saylor wrote on X: "Happy Bitcoin white paper day. 18 years."

One of the most salient features of the whitepaper is the fixed supply of Bitcoin at 21 million coins. The pre-determined issuance structure is what makes Bitcoin different from traditional monetary systems, where central authorities can inflate the money supply.

Major U.S. crypto exchange Coinbase highlighted this fact in its X post: "21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

21,000,000. Never more. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day. https://t.co/JtKeHtCuSM

"Today marks 18 years since the release of the Bitcoin Whitepaper. A day that changed everything," Coinbase continued.

Stablecoin issuer Tether wrote: "On 31 October 2008, Satoshi published nine pages that explained Bitcoin to the world. Today we're explaining it to everyone else. Two pizzas, 10,000 BTC, 21 million coins, and one key you never share. Everything you need to know, in a comic. Happy 18th birthday, Bitcoin whitepaper."

Crypto platform Uphold wrote: "Nine pages that challenged the entire legacy financial system. Happy Bitcoin Whitepaper Day."

The Bitcoin whitepaper laid the groundwork for the network's launch in January 2009, when Satoshi Nakamoto mined Bitcoin's genesis block and introduced the first units of the cryptocurrency.

When Bitcoin launched on January 3, 2009, it had no market value or official exchange price. Over the years, Bitcoin has evolved from a niche technological experiment into a globally recognized digital asset. Its emergence has influenced the development of thousands of cryptocurrencies, blockchain applications, and decentralized financial systems.

The cryptocurrency now trades at $77,310 and is worth $1.55 trillion, according to CoinMarketCap data.

Some blockchains have scheduled mechanisms to distribute burned tokens, but XRP burns are automatic through transaction fees. Every transaction on the XRP Ledger requires a fee denominated in XRP and that fee is burned.

The decline continued on Friday, reaching a low of $1.19 as investors weighed a flurry of economic data and the Federal Reserve's latest interest rate decision of the week.

The key events, including the release of the personal consumption expenditures price index on Thursday, which rose 0.5% monthly and 3.6% year-over-year, exceeding the Fed's 2% target, had impacted the crypto markets alongside the news of Binance's attack, which came a day after the central bank decided to hold its key interest rate steady.

The drop to $1.19 on Friday was met with a rebound, but bulls still didn't gain enough strength to surpass the 200 DMA, with XRP trading below it at press time.

XRP's drop below the 200 DMA raises fresh questions about the cryptocurrency's near-term momentum, but it does not necessarily signal the end of its recovery prospects.

Traders are watching the XRP price action for a hold above the weekly support at the 50 WMA to keep the bullish outlook intact. A breakdown of this support might see XRP targeting $1 or even $0.98. On the other hand, if XRP holds above its weekly support, it might reach $1.70.

In the financial markets, investors are looking ahead to some key jobs data in the coming days, including the October nonfarm payrolls report on Friday.

In a recent update, Binance, through its co-founder Yi He, stated it has allocated $6.34 billion from its own funds to buy up major cryptocurrencies including XRP and RLUSD.

In the current Binance user fund, XRP and RLUSD, alongside other major cryptocurrencies, have now achieved 100% reserve backing.

#5249. Binance’s $6.3B Hack Fix Is Coming Tomorrow: Why the ZK Math Doesn't Tell the Whole Story

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

On-chain data shows the attacker behind the $6.3 billion Binance theft depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses.

At the same time, Binance's first post-hack reserve snapshot shows its biggest assets covered with buffers as small as 2.7 ETH and $6 of USDT. Binance's full zero-knowledge proof of those figures is due by Tuesday.

Some of the money stolen from Binance has started going back to Binance.

Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham has flagged the entity it tracks as "Binance Hacker" depositing about $4 million into three Binance deposit addresses. Arkham says those addresses "likely represent nested service(s)." These are third-party exchanges that use Binance for liquidity and custody, giving their own customers deposit addresses that sit on Binance's infrastructure.

If Arkham is right, the hacker isn't depositing into an ordinary Binance account. The money would be going to smaller platforms that operate through Binance. Exchanges have long known this is a weak point for stolen funds moving into normal trading. Either way, Binance is now receiving stolen funds at its own deposit addresses while it works to show customers it has replaced what was taken.

The FBI has attributed the October 29 theft to North Korea. The deposits come at a sensitive moment. Binance has just published its first reserve snapshot since the hack and has promised a full cryptographic proof of it by Tuesday.

$4 million is a small slice of a theft worth about $6.3 billion, but it matters for two reasons.

It shows how the laundering works. Nested services are a common way into the regulated financial system. A third-party platform that relies on Binance for custody may run weaker identity checks on its own users. Funds deposited there can be swapped and withdrawn without the hacker ever opening a Binance account.

Binance can act on it. Binance can't freeze bitcoin and ether sitting in wallets nobody controls, and it doesn't control the stablecoins that issuers like Tether and Circle have frozen. Deposits that land at its own addresses are different: they are on Binance's platform, so Binance can freeze them itself. One of the first tests of how Binance handles the money still in the hacker's hands is whether it freezes these funds and identifies the services that own the addresses.

While the hacker's funds move, Binance has been rebuilding its reserves. Its proof-of-reserves page now shows:

The first page covers Binance's six largest assets. Customer balances are what users hold. Reserves are on-chain wallet balances, including assets held with outside custodians.

The second page has four more assets, and two of them stand out:

Why USD1 and RLUSD matter: these are two of the stablecoins whose issuers froze stolen funds after the attack. World Liberty Financial froze $27 million of USD1, and Ripple began freezing RLUSD the same night. Both now show reserves above what Binance owes customers.

Assets with outside custodians: part of several reserves sits with outside custodians rather than in Binance's own exchange wallets:

The striking part isn't that the ratios reach 100%. It's how closely they stop there.

Compared with October's report: Binance's previous monthly report, published in early October before the hack, showed BTC at 100.35% and USDT at 103.88%. ETH was already at exactly 100.00%. After the theft:

Not every asset is that tight. USDC, ZEC and BNB carry buffers of 1.3% to 6%. The thinnest buffers are in BTC, ETH, USDT and SOL, which are among the assets the attacker took in the largest amounts.

How Binance says it got here: the pattern fits Binance's account of replacing the stolen assets in stages. It reported 80% replaced on Friday, 90% on Saturday and 95% on Sunday. The remaining 5% is in less-liquid tokens it is still buying. The money came from:

Binance confirmed taking 7,499 BTC from SAFU and has pledged to refill the fund to about $1 billion.

What the snapshot can't show: it was taken a little over a day after the theft, once the rebuild was under way. It shows the balance sheet after the replacement, not how large the gap was on October 29.

Binance says the full proof takes 40 to 50 hours to compute. Its latest update says it will be ready "by Tuesday, 2026-11-03 (UTC)." The system is open source, in Binance's zkmerkle-proof-of-solvency repository.

What the proof guarantees, according to the project's circuit design document:

The design also guards against a "dummy user attack" identified by Ethereum Foundation researcher Enrico Bottazzi. In that attack, fake accounts holding cheap tokens are used to offset debts in major assets.

What it doesn't prove: the reserve side. The project's verifier config describes the totals as information "published by CEX, it represents CEX's liability." The reserve figures are checked a different way, against the wallet addresses Binance publishes through the page's "Download All Address" option.

What customers can do: each user can get a Merkle proof for their account and check it against the published root. They can use the verifier code in Binance's repository rather than Binance's own interface. That doesn't prove Binance is solvent, but it confirms the user's balance was counted.

Binance has rebuilt its reserves to 100% across its ten largest assets, but on several of them the buffer is only a few coins. Meanwhile, stolen funds are reaching its deposit addresses through platforms that run on its infrastructure. Tuesday's proof can confirm customer balances. It can't show how Binance handles the stolen money arriving at its own door.

#5248. Binance to Resume XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum and Other Crypto Withdrawals

Cryptocurrency exchange Binance will allow withdrawals for major cryptocurrencies such as XRP, Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), and Solana (SOL), among others, after suspending withdrawals because of a massive security breach involving $6.3 billion.

Binance announced on Nov. 1 that the exchange would begin resuming withdrawal services between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC.

Binance emphasized that the withdrawal resumption process will be carried out progressively as the exchange conducts security and infrastructure readiness checks.

"We aim to restore withdrawals progressively as we complete security and readiness checks," said Binance.

Binance continued to offer deposit services during the security breach.

The first phase of withdrawal resumption will include a total of 15 blockchain networks.

This list includes popular networks such as Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP Ledger, BNB Smart Chain, Solana, Tron, and Dogecoin.

Other cryptocurrencies that will be available for withdrawals include Zcash (ZEC), Avalanche (AVAX), Sui (SUI), Polygon (POL) and Arbitrum (ARB).

Withdrawals of major stablecoins such as Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) will also be enabled on multiple networks.

The exchange noted that it selected the assets based on user withdrawal demand over the past week.

The exchange also warned that not all listed cryptocurrencies and networks may be enabled at the same time.

The withdrawal resumption comes only days after Binance suffered a massive security breach.

The breach led to the theft of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the exchange's hot wallets.

The exchange temporarily paused withdrawals in order to contain the damage, conduct an investigation into the security breach and avoid additional losses.

Binance has now disclosed that it has recovered around 95% of affected assets.

This is up from 90% when Binance last provided an update on the recovery process.

The exchange said that it has fully backed the balances of cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP, Solana, BNB, USDT, USDC, Zcash, USD1, and Ripple USD (RLUSD).

The remaining 5% includes cryptocurrencies that are less liquid and harder to buy in large amounts.

Bloomberg Intelligence senior commodity strategist Mike McGlone believes that a critical inflection point for Bitcoin (BTC) versus US Treasury bonds could mean a crash for the broader cryptocurrency market.

In a recent post on X, McGlone cautioned that Bitcoin’s ongoing underperformance against US government bonds may have major implications for other asset classes.

“Bitcoin may be backing down at a key inflection point vs. US Treasury bonds, with broad implications for all assets,” McGlone wrote.

Bitcoin Below $80,000 a Sign of Crypto Breakdown vs. T-Bonds Bitcoin may be backing down from a key inflection point vs. US Treasury bonds, with broad implications for all assets. My graphic highlights the iShares Bitcoin ETF (IBIT) potentially rolling over vs. the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT) from a base of 100 at the end of 2024. Bitcoin's dud performance vs. US T-bonds since the end of the milestone year that marked the launch of US ETFs and President Donald Trump's shift to crypto enthusiast from antagonist may signal an end of Bitcoin's glory days. However, Bitcoin hasn’t outperformed traditional government bonds since then.

Per McGlone, the poor performance of the cryptocurrency may mean its best days are in the past.

Citi has revised its price targets for the pioneer cryptocurrency, believing the asset is poised to reclaim $113,000 and even hit $181,000 in the next 12 months.

US Wall Street bank Citi Group made a fresh bold prediction on Bitcoin’s price, now convinced that the asset is set to reach $113,000 before 2027. The $1.2 trillion bank believes the flagship cryptocurrency will rise to $113,000 before the end of the year.

Today, October 1, Citi amended its 12-month Bitcoin price projection from $82,000 to $113,000, a significant shift in its market outlook earlier this year. The latest revision signals the institution’s renewed confidence in the Bitcoin market, supported by positive macroeconomic forces and ETF inflows expected through this year and into 2027.

In January, the bank predicted a price target of $143,000 within the next 12 months. In July, it cut its target from $112,000 to $82,000 when the CLARITY Act lost its momentum in the Senate. During that time, the institution decreased its target, saying that the asset could drop from $112,000 to $82,000 due to negative developments, including consistent ETF outflows, the US’s delayed regulation formulation, and a wider stagnant market.

The latest forecast, issued today, shows that the bank has turned bullish on Bitcoin, believing that the asset is preparing to extend its ongoing recovery in the fourth quarter. While the asset closed Q3 around $82,000, Citi believes the virtual currency is gearing up for a momentum Q4 rally and could reach $113,000 before 2027. The bank expects institutional capital to soon surge into digital assets, suggesting BTC is entering its next bull-run phase.

The Wall Street banking giant expects crypto capital inflows to rise to $5 billion within the next 12 months, driven by the broader market recovery. As a result, the bank believes that Bitcoin’s value could hit $181,000 in the coming 12 months. This price forecast reflects its strong belief that traditional financial institutions are increasingly channeling capital onchain.

Citi’s analysts said Bitcoin is attracting significantly more institutional customers amid economic uncertainty. With heightened institutional demand, major participants like corporate treasuries, pension funds, hedge funds, and others are showing stronger enthusiasm for BTC as a long-term investment.

Citi is convinced that if this momentum continues, BTC could begin a new chapter of adoption, where it’s not only widely used for trading but also as a reserve asset. This transition could push its value to unprecedented heights, with $181,000 a realistic target over the next 12 months.

Notcoin (NOT) began as a viral sensation, pioneering the “tap-to-earn” model on Telegram and onboarding over 35 million users into the TON ecosystem.

However, the initial euphoria gave way to a significant “demise” in market value, as the token plummeted over 95% from its 2024 highs to a current market cap of approximately $39M. This decline was driven by massive airdrop sell pressure and a lack of sustainable utility beyond the initial clicker game.

Today, the NOT token is attempting a “strategic resurgence,” evolving from a simple game into a gaming hub and DeFi platform. It now powers the “Not Games” ecosystem, serves as collateral in DeFi protocols, and even backs a digital Visa card with buyback mechanisms.

Can this pivot from hype to infrastructure restore investor confidence, or was the viral spark a one-time phenomenon? To explore its potential recovery, read our Notcoin price prediction 2026-2030 for a deep dive.

NOT price was crashing like crazy in 2025, but that stopped in 2026 from getting worse.

In 2026, the key price action happened inside the range of $0.00032 to $0.00052. However, based on the NOTUSD (Notcoin) chart, there was an instance in early May 2026 as the price broke through the $0.00060 resistance level. This increase was brief, as the 200-day EMA near $0.00075 resisted the bullish move, causing the NOT price to fall back into the consolidation area below $0.00052.

After being deflected by the 200-day EMA, it returned under these short-term EMA bands in July, and even in August, it stayed under this range.

All of this price action seems like an accumulation phase, but the price is not showing any major momentum.

After mid-August, the price tried to show a rise but still got suppressed by the 200-day EMA band.

But, in September, the NOT price managed to break the 200-day EMA band briefly, but it failed to sustain above it in October.

Now it shows continued consolidation within the range of $0.00032 to $0.00052, with a potential breakdown below this range remaining a distinct possibility.

However, if price shows a recovery and NOT price manages to break past 200-day EMA band then it could break above $0.00060. If, along with that, it manages to break and sustain above the $0.00060 resistance, a bullish trend might start that could push prices higher and eventually revisit levels such as $0.00101, $0.00151, and even $0.00206 by year-end 2026.

On August 5, the community channel ‘cult of NOT’ released a short documentary highlighting “La Confession Booth: the film”, which was an experimental research project by artist in collaboration with ‘Nothing’.

#5243. Do Not Use Your iPhone as Hardware Wallet, OneKey Founder

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Using an old iPhone as a crypto cold wallet may be less safe than it looks, OneKey founder Yishi Wang has warned. The practice is popular with self-custody fans: wipe a spare phone, take it offline, and keep your wallet recovery information on it.

Wang's worry is that an offline phone can still be attacked by someone who has it in their hands. He has pointed to flaws in several generations of iPhone. These include the publicly documented checkm8 issue on older models and, more recently reported, low-level weaknesses in certain later devices. They sit in the early stages of the boot process. A malicious app isn't involved.

An iOS update may not fix a weakness built into immutable boot code. Switching off Wi-Fi and cellular does nothing about someone who gets physical access to the phone. A vulnerability still doesn't automatically mean an attacker can recover a seed phrase, though. Device encryption, passcode strength and secure key handling remain real barriers.

Wang advises against trusting iPhone 11-generation and older devices with recovery phrases. If you think a phrase may have been exposed, create a completely new one using a trusted setup and move your funds to that wallet. Generating another address from the same seed won't help, because the underlying exposure stays.

He also stresses updated operating systems, long alphanumeric passcodes and careful control of USB connections. Earlier, he suggested that even newer iPhones shouldn't be treated as equivalent to purpose-built signing devices when the holdings are substantial and long-term.

Dedicated hardware wallets are built to isolate signing keys and let you check transaction details on the device itself. They carry risk too. Counterfeit hardware, compromised distribution channels and sloppy recovery-phrase handling can all undermine their security.

The argument is about threat models, not brand loyalty. An offline phone cuts remote exposure, but that doesn't turn it into a secure hardware wallet.

Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 70% chance of taking control of both chambers of Congress.

A potential Democratic majority could complicate negotiations over the CLARITY Act and reshape the regulatory outlook for crypto.

AI bailout proposals and the risk of renewed US-Iran strikes add further uncertainty for stocks, oil and global markets.

The US midterm elections on November 3 could become a major market catalyst, with investors watching beyond the battle for control of Congress. Prediction markets currently give Democrats around a 70% chance of winning both the House and Senate. The outcome could influence the direction of AI regulation, the future of crypto legislation and US foreign policy toward Iran.Â

For financial markets, the election carries implications across technology stocks, digital assets, energy prices and inflation. Here are three developments investors should watch as voters head to the polls.

Artificial intelligence has become one of the biggest investment themes on Wall Street, but concerns over elevated valuations, rising infrastructure costs and debt-funded expansion are putting the sector under scrutiny.

On October 29, Democratic lawmakers Maxine Waters and Greg Casar introduced a resolution opposing federal bailouts for AI companies if an AI-related market bubble collapses. The proposal argues that taxpayers should not be required to rescue companies or executives responsible for excessive risk-taking. It also calls for stronger protections for workers, retirees and households exposed to a potential downturn.

A stronger Democratic presence in Congress could increase pressure for greater oversight of AI companies and their financing arrangements. That could add another regulatory consideration for major technology firms investing billions of dollars in data centers, chips and AI infrastructure.

The election could also determine how quickly the US advances comprehensive cryptocurrency regulation. The CLARITY Act, designed to establish a clearer regulatory framework for digital assets, failed to advance in the Senate on September 15. The measure received 49 votes in favor and 50 against, falling short of the 60 votes required. All Democrats and four Republicans opposed advancing the legislation.

A change in congressional control could make negotiations more complicated, particularly if lawmakers disagree over the regulatory responsibilities of the SEC and CFTC, oversight of crypto markets and the treatment of digital asset businesses.

For the crypto industry, regulatory clarity remains an important factor in attracting institutional participation and encouraging US-based companies to expand. A prolonged legislative delay could keep uncertainty elevated for exchanges, token issuers and other digital asset businesses.

Bitcoin and major altcoins may therefore remain sensitive to signals about the next stage of US crypto policy. However, the election outcome alone will not determine the bill’s future; bipartisan support will still be necessary for major legislation to advance.

The geopolitical risk surrounding the election could have an immediate impact on energy markets. US officials have reportedly warned several Middle Eastern allies to prepare for possible renewed military strikes against Iran after November 3. The warnings also include concerns about potential Iranian retaliation against energy facilities and other critical infrastructure. President Donald Trump has not made a final decision on further military action, while diplomatic efforts remain possible.

Any renewed escalation could threaten regional energy infrastructure and disrupt oil supply routes. The Strait of Hormuz remains particularly important because of its role in global energy shipments. Oil markets are already facing considerable supply uncertainty. Brent crude recently settled above $113 per barrel, while US crude traded near $104, with geopolitical tensions and shipping risks adding to market pressure.

A fresh conflict could push oil prices higher, increasing transportation and production costs and adding pressure to global inflation. That could complicate the Federal Reserve’s policy decisions and weigh on risk-sensitive assets, including equities and cryptocurrencies.

The November 3 election will provide the first indication of how political control in Washington could change, but its market implications will extend beyond the initial results.

A Democratic victory in both chambers could bring tougher scrutiny of AI financing and complicate negotiations over crypto legislation. Meanwhile, the possibility of renewed military action against Iran creates a separate risk for oil supplies, inflation and global market sentiment.

For investors, the key will be how quickly these political developments translate into policy decisions. Technology stocks, crypto assets and energy markets could each respond differently, making the election an important event for financial markets heading into the final months of 2026 and beyond.

Validator support for the fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment must stay above 80% for it to activate. If it slips to 80% or lower even once, the amendment is rejected and the 14-day timer starts over.

This fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment is essential for Permission Delegation, which went live in October, as until it is enabled, users would not be able to delegate the PaymentBurn granular permission.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. A reported $1.1 billion in NEAR Protocol derivatives open interest has put the spotlight on speculative positioning in the token. The exact figure and its timing need confirmation at the exchange level. The general point holds either way: leveraged trading magnifies both optimism and downside when interest in an asset picks up.

Open interest is the notional value of futures and perpetual futures contracts that are still open. Daily trading volume is something else, a count of transactions over a period. Rising open interest means more positions are staying active. It doesn't say whether traders as a group expect prices to rise or fall, since every contract has exposure on both sides.

NEAR's derivatives participation has been swining before. In October open interest climbed above $1 billion and approached $1.9 billion during a strong price rally, then a pullback.

To read a fresh increase, analysts usually compare open interest with spot price, funding rates, trading volume and liquidation data. When price and open interest rise together, the market often reads that as growing risk appetite. If prices fall while open interest stays high, crowded leveraged positions become vulnerable to forced exits.

Funding rates are just another source of data. Sustained positive funding can suggest stronger demand for leveraged longs, and negative funding a preference for shorts. Neither is conclusive alone, and differences between exchanges can muddy comparisons.

NEAR's longer-term prospects depend on more than derivatives. Transaction costs, ecosystem integrations and adoption of cross-chain infrastructure such as NEAR Intents are more longer-term drivers. Speculative positioning can move the price fast, but it is no substitute for durable demand for blockchain services.

New leveraged positions must be backed by spot-market buying and healthy liquidity in order to have relevance. A large open-interest figure shows attention, nothing more. It isn't a forecast. Check it across data providers and manage risk carefully.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The cryptocurrency market is breaking the classical rules of financial economics. The industry has faced the biggest challenge in its history: the FBI confirmed that North Korean hackers attacked Binance's infrastructure and withdrew $6.3 billion.

However, instead of a protracted capitulation, this news triggered a paradoxical reaction: prices held, creating a strong bullish precedent.

Against this backdrop, well-known crypto analyst DonAlt, who accurately predicted the historic 700% XRP rally back in 2024, directly cites the Binance hack as the reason for his ultra-bullish sentiment. In his opinion, in the current situation it is "hard to be a bear" precisely because of how the market reacted to the catastrophe.

The situation was promptly stabilized by the actions of the platform itself, which acted proactively and covered 90% of users' lost funds from its own reserves, and by the Treasury Department. As a result, Bitcoin ignored attempts at mass sell-offs and held around $77,935, while XRP settled at $1.2498.

The main indicator for the analyst was the complete absence of panic follow-through selling after the shocking news. DonAlt draws a direct analogy with the events of November 2022, when the industry was going through the collapse of the FTX exchange:

"Last time the market didn't properly sell off after a huge event like this was the FTX collapse. When I saw the lack of follow through then I got giga bullish. And we subsequently went from 16k to 100k. Hard to be bearish here after having been given the same setup yet again"

The expert emphasizes that there are no 100% guarantees in financial markets and classifies the current situation as a game of mathematical probabilities. According to him, when the market prices in colossal negativity but refuses to go down, the odds in the long run are always on the side of buyers.

Still, DonAlt’s argument rests on a single precedent. The FTX analogy worked once, but one case is not a pattern, and the two events differ in important ways. FTX wiped out customer funds for good, while in the Binance case most losses were covered within days.

A market that does not fall on a compensated hack is responding rationally, not necessarily showing hidden strength.

The real test will come in the next few weeks: if prices hold once the news is fully priced in and attention shifts to the stolen funds moving through mixers, the bullish case gets much stronger. If they don’t, the lack of follow-through may turn out to have been only a delay.

#5236. Why Didn't Bitcoin Drop More? Binance's CZ Credits FBI

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao (CZ) credited the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) and other US law enforcement agencies with helping prevent a larger drop in the Bitcoin (BTC) price after the massive $6.3 billion security breach at the Binance cryptocurrency exchange.

Binance founder CZ commended the timely actions of the FBI, US Secret Service (USSS), and Internal Revenue Service (IRS) amid the massive security breach.

According to CZ's Nov. 1 post on X, US law enforcement agencies (FBI, USSS, IRS and more) helped "a lot" during the incident.

For instance, they helped with tracking and freezing funds.

According to the Binance co-founder, they were able to prevent an even sharper fall in the Bitcoin price.

"Not enough to express our appreciation in a tweet. There are probably a lot of crypto bros not realizing that a lot of 'why bitcoin didn't drop even more?' credits go to them," CZ stated.

This comes after the FBI officially identified North Korean hackers as being behind the record-breaking Binance hack.

According to the FBI's Oct. 31 announcement, North Korea stole more than $6 billion worth of cryptocurrencies from the Binance crypto exchange on or about Oct. 29.

More specifically, the FBI identified the North Korean cybercrime group TraderTraitor as being behind the massive cryptocurrency theft.

It's a known North Korean hacker group that has stolen large amounts of cryptocurrencies before.

The FBI noted that investigators, together with the Secret Service and IRS Criminal Investigation, have tracked how the hackers were exchanging stolen cryptocurrencies mainly for Ethereum (ETH).

The FBI warned that these assets could be further laundered using decentralized finance (DeFi) protocols and instant cryptocurrency swap services.

The US authorities have called on cryptocurrency businesses and infrastructure providers to block transactions related to the cryptocurrency addresses used by the hackers to stop them from laundering these assets.

Specifically, the US authorities urged THORNode operators, remote procedure call (RPC) node operators, instant exchanges, blockchain analytics companies, DeFi platforms, etc., to block such transactions.

Apart from that, the FBI provided a list of the cryptocurrency addresses used by the hackers to allow other members of the cryptocurrency industry to detect and block suspicious transactions.

The Binance security breach sent shock waves throughout the cryptocurrency market.

Bitcoin tumbled below $77,000 after the market reacted to the unprecedented crypto theft.

BTC dropped to around $76,000 at one point, registering its lowest price in several weeks.

Meanwhile, other major cryptocurrencies like Ethereum, XRP, Solana (SOL), and BNB nosedived as the market reacted to the breach.

Fortunately, Bitcoin eventually found stability and was trading around $78,000 during the early Nov. 1 trading session.

This collaborative approach makes it easier for local tech firms and finance-focused institutions based in Japan to utilize the Cardano blockchain for business applications. By leveraging Cardano’s smart contracts, companies in the Pacific Meta consortium can streamline operations, reduce costs, improve security, and tap into new on-chain opportunities for growth and innovation.

Solana price faces continued selling pressure as a large whale deposits 1.49 million SOL worth nearly $148.77 million into exchanges.

Spot Solana ETFs record approximately $71.47 million in weekly outflows, signalling weaker institutional demand.

SOL trades below key moving averages, with $88 emerging as an important support level.

Solana price is struggling to reclaim the $100 mark as selling pressure continues to weigh on the cryptocurrency. Large whale transfers to exchanges, persistent withdrawals from spot Solana ETFs and weakening technical momentum are creating a challenging environment for buyers. The token has also extended its losing streak, raising concerns about whether the current correction could deepen.

Three factors are putting pressure on SOL and could determine whether it manages to recover or faces another leg lower.

Large-scale whale activity is one of the latest concerns for Solana investors. On-chain data shared by Lookonchain shows that an unidentified whale deposited approximately 1.49 million SOL, worth around $148.77 million, into multiple cryptocurrency exchanges over the past 10 days.

This mysterious whale keeps dumping $SOL!Over the past 10 days, the whale has deposited 1.49M $SOL ($148.77M) into multiple exchanges.https://t.co/zZFhaOfFX1https://t.co/p31EM5Ma1Z pic.twitter.com/sX5ijDbYFV

The transfers involved several major platforms, including Binance, Coinbase, OKX, Kraken, Bybit and Bitstamp. Moving such a large amount of SOL to exchanges has raised concerns about potential selling pressure, particularly as the token struggles to hold above $100.

The activity follows an earlier update on October 29, when the same whale was reported to have deposited approximately 1.02 million SOL worth $104.3 million over five days. The latest figures suggest that the transfers have continued.

Institutional investment flows are providing another challenge for Solana. US-listed spot Solana ETFs recorded approximately $71.47 million in net outflows last week, marking their largest weekly withdrawals since launch.

The withdrawals also extended the fund category’s outflow streak to four consecutive weeks, indicating that institutional investors have become more cautious toward SOL.

ETF flows are closely watched because they offer insight into demand from traditional market participants. Sustained outflows can weaken the demand supporting an asset, particularly when broader market conditions are already negative. A return to consistent inflows could help stabilize sentiment, but continued withdrawals may leave the token vulnerable to further selling.

Solana’s price structure has also weakened after its recent decline. The daily chart shows SOL falling from its earlier highs and returning to an important support region after failing to sustain its recovery. The token is trading below its 50-day EMA near $103.81, 100-day EMA around $99.96 and 200-day EMA near $98.08. These moving averages now form an overhead resistance zone, making a sustained move above $100 increasingly important for buyers.

On the upside, SOL needs to reclaim the $98â$100 region before targeting the $103â$104 resistance zone. A successful move above these levels could signal improving momentum. However, the $88.42 area remains the key downside support. A decisive break below this zone could expose the next major support near $78.35. The daily RSI is approaching oversold territory, but the negative MACD suggests bearish momentum has not yet clearly reversed.

Solana’s recovery depends on whether buyers can absorb the selling pressure from large holders and restore demand through institutional investment. A move above $100 would be an early positive signal, followed by the $103â$104 resistance zone.

On the other hand, continued whale deposits and ETF outflows could keep SOL under pressure. A breakdown below $88.42 would increase the risk of a deeper correction toward $78.35.

#5233. 1.8 Billion XRP Moves in Just 24 Hours as XRP Ledger Shows Signs of Recovery

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

A headline claiming that 1.8 billion XRP moved across the XRP Ledger within 24 hours has revived discussion of a network recovery. The figure hasn't been independently verified for a dated 24-hour period, so treat it as a reported claim, not confirmed evidence of a new trend.

The XRP Ledger handles payments, decentralized exchange transactions and tokenized assets. Payment volumes reflects the network activity, but the number needs context. Large transfers can be exchange custody movements, internal treasury operations or transfers between wallets controlled by the same entity.

None of that necessarily signals fresh investor demand or new capital entering the market.

Recent verified reporting shows why the distinction matters. One October snapshot had daily payment volume jumping to about 137.7 million XRP, still below its 30-day average of roughly 496 million.

Another October reading, around 363.3 million XRP, came with the same caution: a one-day rise did not establish a sustained recovery.

A reading near 1.8 billion XRP usually comes at the end of the week where most of the network activity occurs. The most likely outcome is always the same: high activity by Thursday and Friday and a tubmling on the weekend, with a recovery starting on Monday.

Other indicators help separate real adoption from a passing spike: active addresses, successful payment counts, decentralized-exchange trading, liquidity and how transaction sizes are distributed. Even high transaction counts can mislead when automated activity dominates, as recent investigations into small-value stablecoin payments on XRPL showed.

Network usage and XRP's market price are only indirectly related. More settlement activity doesn't guarantee higher token prices, and speculative buying can lift prices with no matching improvement in usage. Broader market conditions and exchange liquidity matter too.

A verified natural burst of XRP movement could mean renewed engagement with the network. A more convincing signal would be several consecutive days of stronger, widely distributed activity, backed by improving liquidity and sustained user demand, which rarely happens.

In late October 2026, Zcash (ZEC) reached a key milestone: the coin's price consolidated around $1,280, and its market capitalization hit $21.8 billion. However, the rapid rally was overshadowed by a sharp split within the community.

The trigger of the crisis was not a technical problem but a revolt of large investors over the targeted spending of capital.

Zcash Community Grants (ZCG), the organization that distributes part of the miners' block reward, launched the Zcash Adoption Pool program. The fund directed grants toward the integration of vulnerable groups like refugees without access to banks.

The decision sparked protest from major players, since ZCG's charter allows it to distribute multimillion-dollar budgets bypassing the coinholder vote. The "whale" revolt moved into the practical realm: a major holder under the pseudonym "big z" publicly announced a full sell-off of his ZEC holdings.

According to him, the fund should finance cryptography, not political manifestos.

The local conflict quickly grew into a debate about the nature of decentralized money, which industry heavyweights joined. Developer Sean Bowe published a manifesto on the future of ZCG, in which he called for revising the fund's financing due to the anomalous surge in the ZEC price.

The initiative was unexpectedly supported by legendary investor Naval Ravikant, who laconically snapped that a $50 million cap is more than enough for community grants.

Meanwhile, the fund's activists continue to insist that private money is a "humanitarian imperative" and a public good.

However, Gemini exchange co-founder Tyler Winklevoss harshly challenged this thesis: a commercial network with transaction fees cannot be a public good. Winklevoss compared ZCG's actions to "taxation without representation" and called for leaving the development of Zcash to the free market.

The pressure on the price from the whales' coin sell-off coincided with the launch of direct ZEC deposits on the decentralized Rujira Network on October 29.

After failing to break above $1,390, the price settled in the $1,220–1,245 $range, still well below the all-time high of $1,698 set in late September. The fundamental dispute over who should control Zcash's millions remains open.

According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, the Binance hacker has dumped more than 130 altcoins across EVM chains, generating about $279 million in proceeds.

A security incident at digital asset exchange Binance last Thursday affected some $6.3 billion in assets, making it the largest crypto theft on record. Binance's initial investigation suggested the security incident may have started with a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions.

How many altcoins has the Binance hacker dumped? On EVM chains alone, the hacker dumped over 130 altcoins, receiving: 123,400 $ETH ($277.26M) 1.69M $USDC Total: $279M https://t.co/Y8JYpWRP73

In a recent analysis on X, Lookonchain examined how many altcoins the Binance hacker has dumped. It noted that on EVM chains alone, the hacker dumped over 130 altcoins, sharing the list of some tokens affected in a table including SHIB. The hacker dumped 499,926,072,560 SHIB with a selling value of 873 ETH worth $1,960,615.

In return for the altcoins sold, the hacker received 123,400 ETH worth $277.26 million and 1.69 million USDC, totaling approximately $279 million.

The Binance hacker continues to swap stolen funds. In a recent report by Lookonchain, the hacker is swapping the stolen 970,522 SOL worth $95.9 million for BTC.

As reported, the over 499 billion SHIB stolen in the Binance hack represented 0.05% of its supply, with the SHIB price relatively absorbing the selloff.

Shiba Inu price saw a sharp selloff on October 29, alongside the rest of the crypto market in an initial reaction to the news of the Binance hack. The drop hit a low of $0.00000446 on Friday, from where SHIB sharply rebounded. Shiba Inu closed Saturday in the red, marking a loss of 18.92% in October.

Shiba Inu rebounded thereafter, fluctuating between $0.00000466 and $0.00000472 on November's first day as the price awaits further direction. At the time of writing, SHIB was down 0.04% in the last 24 hours to $0.00000469 and down 3.14% weekly.

Binance says it has replenished about 95% of the impacted assets, reiterating a clear commitment to absorb the financial impact of the stolen funds. The crypto exchange also said it will continue to buy the remaining relevant token assets through market and over-the-counter channels until the covered amount reaches 100% for all tokens.

The rapid growth of the sector is largely tied to how the digital assets themselves are structured. At the moment, 86% of tokenized stocks are issued under the model of classic stablecoins: the instruments are fully backed by the underlying asset in a 1:1 ratio and, at the same time, function without the direct operational or legal participation of the issuer of the original securities.

Professional market participants assess this shift as a potential repetition of the success of stablecoins, but this time in the stock market.

While spot infrastructure is being built on Ethereum, a completely different, speculative life is unfolding in the derivatives market. Here, historical records are being set on decentralized venues: open interest, with contracts on the same tokenized stocks accounting for the largest share, has reached $1.76 billion.

An example of this ecosystem is the Hyperliquid platform, whose native token HYPE is trading at around $87.70. The coin is supported by an inflow of new holders, as well as automated tokenomics: the platform directs $1.24 million daily to buying back HYPE from the open market.

Representatives of the investment community have outlined the zone from $70 to $76 as a key long-term support level. Current market conditions point to a possible move toward the $90–$100 range.

The existence of this parallel reality — from spot on Ethereum to highly liquid futures on Hyperliquid — shows that the blockchain is becoming a multi-level environment for different types of capital.

Injective Institutional Rail gives banks and enterprises a dedicated connection to block production.

Transactions enter an Enterprise Validator's mempool for priority inclusion, while the full validator set finalizes blocks.

The rail is already in production with selected institutions and supports Injective's regulated tokenization strategy.

Injective has introduced Institutional Rail, a dedicated connection for banks and enterprises seeking access to its block production. The system is designed to provide predictable transaction inclusion and instant finality, addressing a familiar institutional concern: uncertain execution timing.

Instead of relying on public endpoints, participating firms send transactions directly into an Enterprise Validator’s mempool for priority inclusion in the next block. The full validator set still votes on and finalizes every block.

8/ Institutional Rail is already in production across a select group of financial institutions and major enterprise teams.Read the full announcement and request early access:https://t.co/x81W21wfG4

The setup offers more than a place in the transaction queue. Injective Institutional Rail also returns an optimistic execution result before block commit, allowing financial firms to prepare subsequent orders sooner.

Treasury teams can update internal systems or flag exceptions earlier. Meanwhile, Injective’s exchange module uses batch auctions, where matching orders clear at a uniform price. Institutional orders still compete with other participants on the same network.

That distinction matters. Priority access doesn’t mean institutions operate outside the shared market.

The Enterprise Validator runs on secure hardware with remote attestation. Firms retain custody of their own keys and assets, while the broader validator set remains responsible for block finalization.

Injective identifies Google Cloud, Deutsche Telekom, Kraken, and BitGo among major partner institutions participating in its validator ecosystem.

Institutional Rail is already in production with selected financial institutions and enterprise teams. For Injective, the real test now is whether predictable execution can translate into broader institutional adoption.

#5223. Why Coinbase Bitcoin Discount Just Hit a Yearly High

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Classic crypto market metrics have suddenly stopped reflecting reality. Bitcoin’s discount on the U.S. exchange Coinbase relative to the international Binance has hit a yearly high, with the Coinbase Premium Index collapsing to around −0.06%.

In normal times, such a chart gives traders a cold sweat: the index going deep into the red zone means that large funds in the U.S. have started massively dumping crypto.

However, the current collapse of the indicator turned out to be a technical illusion. It was provoked by the emergency freeze of operations on Binance immediately after a large-scale hack of the exchange, which completely blocked classic cross-exchange arbitrage.

The anomalous price gap coincided with the largest incident in the industry’s history: on October 29–30, hackers attacked Binance’s hot wallets, withdrawing about $6.3 billion. The exchange promptly froze half of the stolen funds on the blockchain, and the head of the platform promised to fully cover the remaining client losses from the SAFU reserve fund.

Nevertheless, amid the panic, the price of Bitcoin dropped to $77,000–$78,000.

To localize the problem, Binance completely shut the gateways — it temporarily banned any deposits and withdrawals of funds. This decision instantly paralyzed cross-exchange arbitrage. Large players physically could not buy the temporarily cheaper Bitcoin on Coinbase and transfer it to Binance to even out the price.

Liquidity was locked inside the platforms, which caused the discount to artificially swell to its widest level in a year.

As noted by Galaxy Research’s head of research Alex Thorn, due to the blocking of transactions, the discount on Coinbase temporarily stopped being a signal of weak demand in the U.S.

On November 1, Binance announced a phased reopening of withdrawals, starting with BTC and ETH. Now the market is waiting to see how quickly arbitrageurs eliminate the gap. If the gap closes in the coming days, it means the anomaly was purely technical.

If the negative spread becomes entrenched, it will be an alarming signal of a real cooling of American capital.

#5222. Nvidia, Nike and 48 Other Companies Oppose OKX Stock Tokenization Plan

A total of 50 companies, including Nvidia (NVDA) and Nike (NKE), have officially raised objections to the trading of tokenized shares on a new platform backed by crypto exchange OKX and the parent company of the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE).

As per the most recent public notice by the joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), OKXICE, the total number of companies objecting to the initiative has reached 50 as of Oct. 30.

The total increased from 38 companies on Oct. 28, with 12 additional companies raising objections in just two days.

The new names that recently raised objections include Nvidia, Nike, Costco (COST), Micron Technology (MU) and Reddit (RDDT).

Other companies that have recently raised objections include cybersecurity firm CrowdStrike (CRWD), Corning (GLW), Bloom Energy (BE), IREN (IREN), USA Rare Earth (USAR), Palo Alto Networks (PANW) and Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE).

Big names in the financial world, including JPMorgan Chase (JPM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and Wells Fargo (WFC), have also raised objections.

Some other prominent names include Walmart (WMT), Coca-Cola (KO), McDonald's (MCD), Eli Lilly (LLY), Adobe (ADBE) and Dell Technologies (DELL).

OKXICE is a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and Intercontinental Exchange (ICE). Each of them owns a 50% stake in the joint venture.

The goal is to enable tokenized versions of traditional US stocks to be traded on the blockchain.

Instead of buying these shares on a traditional brokerage platform, eligible investors can trade blockchain tokens that represent ownership interests in the underlying securities.

The platform will be open 24 hours a day, seven days a week, as per the company's public notice.

The planned platform will be based on a temporary regulatory exemption issued by the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) on Sept. 17.

However, the regulator gave companies the option to object to any unauthorized third-party tokenization of their shares.

If a company submits an objection within the specified timeframe, then its third-party tokenized shares cannot be offered by the platform under the exemption.

#5220. 40 Million XRP Moved From Binance Hacker Wallet

Blockchain tracking service Whale Alert has reported that a wallet linked to the massive $6.3 billion Binance hack has just sent 40 million XRP (~$50.5 million) to a mystery address.

On Nov. 2, Whale Alert shared information about the huge XRP transfer, noting that the transaction initiator is an address tagged "Binance Hack 2026."

The huge transfer took place at 03:56 UTC, Whale Alert data shows. The transaction involved 40 million XRP (~$50.46 million).

Interestingly, just 50 seconds before that, Whale Alert reported another transfer of 40 million XRP.

Another 40 million XRP (~$50.44 million) was also sent from the wallet tagged as "Binance Hack 2026" to a mystery address.

In total, these two transfers involved 80 million XRP (~$100.9 million).

Both transfers originated from the same wallet but were sent to separate mystery addresses.

It is still unclear why these transfers were made. There is no sign that these funds have been sent to a crypto exchange or sold yet.

The transactions took place just days after Binance faced one of the biggest cryptocurrency hacks ever.

The massive XRP transfers came shortly after Binance started to restore cryptocurrency withdrawals following the unprecedented security breach the cryptocurrency exchange faced.

On Nov. 1, Binance annonced that the exchange would restore withdrawals in phases for 15 blockchain networks, including XRP Ledger, Bitcoin, Ethereum, BNB Smart Chain and Solana.

It also mentioned that withdrawals would be gradually restored for other networks, such as Tron, Dogecoin, Zcash, Avalanche, Sui, Polygon and Arbitrum.

The first stage of withdrawal resumption was set to take place between 06:00 and 09:00 UTC on Nov. 1.

After Binance faced a security breach on Oct. 29, which led to the loss of around $6.3 billion worth of cryptocurrency from its hot wallets, it temporarily paused withdrawals.

The exchange noted that withdrawals would be restored gradually after the security and infrastructure checks had been performed.

Binance also said that XRP balances were already fully backed, as were those of other major cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and BNB.

Binance claimed that, as of Nov. 1, around 95% of affected assets had been replenished. The remaining 5% consists primarily of less liquid cryptocurrencies.

#5217. Hackers Use Claude, Gemini and Kimi to Identify Valuable Crypto Targets

Cybercriminals are using popular artificial intelligence (AI) models like Anthropic's Claude, Google's Gemini and Moonshot AI's Kimi AI to evaluate the financial worth of potential victims, including those owning cryptocurrencies.

Cybersecurity researchers at Cisco Talos detailed in a new report how a new type of Windows malware dubbed VOLTA-AUTODOXER, or simply VOLTA, steals sensitive data and uses AI tools to identify potentially lucrative targets among compromised users.

Compared to traditional information-stealing malware, which mainly steals passwords and credentials, VOLTA can also analyze stolen data to build victim profiles and determine what assets hackers can potentially exploit for profit.

Notably, one of VOLTA's most dangerous features is its ability to extract sensitive crypto wallet information, including recovery seed phrases, which can potentially give attackers access to digital assets.

VOLTA also includes features that can crack cryptocurrency wallet vaults, posing a big risk for people who store their crypto wallet credentials on their computers.

But its features are not just limited to stealing crypto.

As explained by Cisco Talos security researcher Ryan Fetterman, VOLTA can also grab saved browser passwords, payment card info, authentication tokens, email credentials and active sessions on popular platforms like Telegram, Discord, Steam and Roblox.

It can also extract info from Outlook accounts and Slack workspaces, as well as other personal and professional information on the infected system.

The malware also takes things further by analyzing victims' email accounts to grab more personal data.

For example, it can scan Gmail accounts for purchase confirmations and receipts from services like Amazon, PayPal, Walmart, DoorDash and Uber Eats.

This way, attackers can get more details about a victim's identity, home address, job and spending habits.

The malware can send stolen data to AI models via the OpenRouter service, which provides access to several AI models.

It first tries to process the collected data using Anthropic's Claude Opus 4.6.

If the model fails to process the request, VOLTA is hardcoded to try Moonshot AI's Kimi K2 and Google's Gemini 2.5 Flash.

As explained by Cisco Talos, VOLTA specifically looks for refusal responses before attempting to use a different AI model.

It feeds the collected data to the AI models and asks them to analyze it, providing a comprehensive evaluation of a victim's financial worth.

It can also help identify valuable assets and then rank them based on how lucrative they may be. It can also score a victim's cybersecurity.

Essentially, it allows hackers to use AI models to find potentially lucrative targets without the need to manually sift through stolen data.

The compromised hot wallet of the Binance exchange has been completely emptied. Blockchain tracker Whale Alert recorded two identical transactions of 40 million XRP each (around $101 million in total), which went to a new address 50 seconds apart.

This is the platform's corporate address rK21t6nGLy4MNDqhvy3pGwcLFy25qgfzMx. After the October 29 attack, the wallet received an official red "Reported as hacked" label in network explorers.

As a result of this final transfer, the address's balance dropped to 23.7 XRP (around $30) — the exchange fully removed the remaining funds, moving them to new internal wallets.

This transfer effectively closes activity on the vulnerable address and is a planned technical consolidation of the remaining balances. The transfer of assets followed a large-scale cross-chain attack on Binance that began on October 29. Total damage across ten different blockchains is estimated at $6.3 billion, making the incident the largest crypto theft in history.

Hot wallets on the XRP Ledger took the first hit: within five minutes at the start of the attack, a total of 233.46 million XRP (around $296 million) was withdrawn from them.

The specifics of the XRPL network itself oblige the exchange to fully zero out hacked addresses. Unlike most stablecoins (such as USDT or USDC), where issuers can forcibly freeze funds, the XRP Ledger code has no protocol-level blocking function.

Neither Ripple nor independent XRP Ledger developers has no technical ability to stop transactions, so leaving any available balance on a hacked wallet is unsafe. Moving the remaining 80 million XRP to new wallets isolated by the platform eliminates the risk of repeated withdrawals.

For the XRP ecosystem, this incident became an absolute all-time negative record, surpassing the September hack of the Bitget exchange, in which 103 million XRP ($157 million) was lost, multiple times over.

At the same time, no panic has been recorded on the market. Binance has fully restored withdrawal operations for clients. The platform's management officially stated that all net user losses will be compensated 1:1 from corporate reserves and SAFU fund money.

The transfer of the last $101 million in XRP likely puts an end to operations with the hacked address, minimizing further technical risks for the platform.

#5213. Fed Meeting Today: Traders Price a 95% Hold and a 79% December Hike. What Does It Mean for Crypto?

Fed meeting today: markets give a hold 95% odds and a December hike 79%. What traders expect from Warsh and what it means for Bitcoin.

The Federal Reserve is expected to keep its policy rate at 3.75% to 4.00% when its two-day Fed meeting ends on Wednesday, October 28, as officials weigh 3.7% inflation against a weakening job market six days before the U.S. midterms. Polymarket traders give a hold 94.9% odds ahead of the 2 p.m. ET statement. The decision itself is mostly priced in. December isn’t: the same markets see a 79% chance of another hike then, so crypto traders will be watching Chair Kevin Warsh’s press conference at 2:30 p.m. more than the statement.

Bitcoin trades at $81,430, up 1.9% in 24 hours.

A hold is close to certain, and the betting is now on December. Prediction markets, futures and economists line up:

Polymarket’s October market alone has drawn $86 million in bets. Its most likely three-meeting path, at 59%, is a hold today, a hike in December and a hold in January. The December figures add the 25 and 50 basis-point hike markets on each platform.

The bond market agrees. The two-year Treasury yield stood at 4.68% on Monday, 68 basis points above the top of the Fed’s range and up from 4.17% in late August. Traders don’t demand that much more than the Fed pays unless they expect it to keep raising rates.

A hawkish hold: no move today, but no promise of a pause either. The case for waiting is that the data are pulling in two directions. September’s consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier, up from 3.4% in August, with Brent crude still near $111 a barrel. At the same time, employers added just 29,000 jobs in September and unemployment rose to 4.2%.

The Fed raised rates by a quarter point on September 16, by a 12–0 vote. Its statement said inflation was still too high and that “the Committee will deliver price stability.” Warsh has largely avoided forward guidance as chair and has said he doesn’t “prejudge meetings.”

The number to watch is the dissents. Cleveland’s Beth Hammack, Dallas’s Lorie Logan and Minneapolis’s Neel Kashkari voted for a hike in July, when the rest of the committee held. On Polymarket, two dissents are the most likely outcome at 33.5%, ahead of three (28%) and none (23%). Matt Weller of FOREX.com calls two or more dissents a “true hawkish hold,” while zero would cast doubt on December.

Timing adds a political layer. “The Fed doesn’t want to poke the White House in the eye six days before an election,” SMBC chief economist Joseph LaVorgna said ahead of the meeting.

The most plausible outcome is a hold with two hawkish dissents, a statement that again calls inflation too high, and a press conference in which Warsh keeps December open without committing to it. That would leave the December odds roughly where they are, between 73% and 79%. The bigger surprise risk is on the dovish side: no dissents, or Warsh arguing that 5% ten-year yields are already doing the Fed’s work.

History this year says the reaction matters more than the decision. Bitcoin after each 2026 Fed decision. Source: Binance

That leaves room for a surprise in either direction. A firm signal for December would lift yields and the dollar, which has tended to weigh on Bitcoin. A softer Warsh would do the opposite.

The calendar doesn’t end tonight. September’s PCE inflation and third-quarter GDP arrive on Thursday, Deribit’s monthly options expire on Friday, and the midterms follow on November 3.

New account creation on the XRP Ledger jumped 142.4%, according to XRPScan data. It points to renewed interest in the ecosystem, even though XRP is still struggling to get its bullish momentum back.

XRPScan counted 7,734 newly activated accounts on November 1, 2026, up 33% from the day before and far above the network's 30-day average of roughly 3,500 new accounts a day.

Wallet creation is clearly speeding up. What's behind it is still unclear.

There are a few plausible explanations. Interest in tokenized assets, stablecoins, and decentralized finance apps on the XRPL may be pushing people to set up new wallets. Exchange onboarding and automated wallet creation could also be adding to the count.

But more accounts doesn't necessarily mean more users. One person can open several accounts, and automated systems can open many more, so other on-chain indicators are needed to judge real adoption.

XRPScan's history also shows account creation has spiked before, with an all-time high of about 30,600 accounts. The latest jump is well short of that.

The network numbers are growing, but the price paints a different picture.

TradingView data from November 2 shows XRP trading near $1.25, after a long correction from its September and October highs. It is still below several major moving averages, so bearish pressure continues to dominate the technical picture.

Immediate support sits around $1.20–$1.25. If XRP tries to recover, the $1.30-$1.35 region could act as resistance.

Rising account creation alongside falling prices reflects blockchain adoption and market demand, which are not the same thing. Stronger confirmation of growing XRPL adoption would need sustained growth in active addresses, transaction volumes, and general use of the ecosystem.

For now, the 142.4% increase is an encouraging sign of network activity. Whether it turns into real demand for XRP is still an open question.

#5211. Ripple’s Bank Approval Leaves XRP On The Sidelines?

Home » Trendsetter News » Ripple’s Bank Approval Leaves XRP On The Sidelines?

Ripple’s bank approval advances its custody and stablecoin business, but may not translate into immediate XRP demand.

XRP funds recorded a $3.61 million net outflow on the day Ripple reportedly secured final approval for its national trust bank. That disconnect anchors a video by crypto commentator Dana Love, who argues the charter primarily advances Ripple’s stablecoin business—not immediate demand for XRP.

Love puts XRP near $1.29 on the reported October 26 approval date and around $1.32 two days later. Over the preceding 30 days, the token had fallen 14.74%, despite a flurry of Ripple announcements around its Swell conference.

The distinction starts with what the bank would actually do. Citing an Office of the Comptroller of the Currency approval letter, Love says Ripple National Trust Bank would provide institutional cryptocurrency custody and manage reserves backing RLUSD, Ripple’s dollar stablecoin.

It would not issue RLUSD itself, accept conventional deposits or make loans. Love describes it as “a vault with a federal badge on the door”—regulated infrastructure, rather than a mechanism that automatically creates token demand.

He also argues that much of the approval was already anticipated. According to the YouTube video research, the OCC conditionally approved Ripple’s application on December 12, 2025, alongside four others; final authorization marked completion of the remaining requirements.

A more direct development for XRP holders, Love says, was BNY’s expanded custody support. He cites a Ripple announcement naming both XRP and RLUSD on BNY’s digital-asset custody platform, potentially removing an operational hurdle for institutions considering the token.

The video cites approximately $1.81 billion in cumulative net inflows into spot XRP ETFs, but just $4.3 million during October 19–23. The reported charter-day withdrawal was followed by a session with no net flows.

Love also questions headlines describing large-wallet concentration as investor accumulation. Two wallets he examined, labeled Ripple 10 and Ripple 11, each received 500 million XRP from escrow. Those balances, he argues, should not be confused with fresh purchases by independent investors.

His outlook remains explicitly speculative: he assigns an 85% probability that an outside institution publicly names Ripple’s bank as its RLUSD custodian by June 30, 2027, versus 20% for XRP custody.

For investors, the distinction is practical: Ripple can expand its regulated business without producing equivalent buying pressure for XRP. Named custody clients and sustained fund inflows would offer stronger evidence of token demand than the charter alone.
