#5210. Bitcoin ETFs Take In $424 Million, but BTC Slips Below $80,000: What Bitcoin News Could November Bring?

Bitcoin news: ETFs took in $424M in three days, yet BTC fell under $80,000 after a split Fed hold. Bitcoin rose in only 3 of 8 Novembers.

U.S. spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds took in $137.3 million on Wednesday, October 28, their third straight day of inflows, while the Federal Reserve held interest rates at 3.75% to 4% and two of its officials voted for a hike. The buying didn’t hold the price for long. Bitcoin rose to $81,788 after the decision, then fell to $79,710 overnight as a selloff in chip stocks spread to crypto.

BTC trades at $79,899, down 1.2% in 24 hours and 4.4% for October, which is on track to be its second losing October in a row. For traders following Bitcoin news into November, the calendar is crowded: the midterm elections, fresh jobs and inflation data, and a December rate hike that prediction markets now price at 79%.

So what do the ETF flows, the Fed and November’s record say?

Lisa Cook and Beth Hammack voted for an increase. pic.twitter.com/nUKDM6n8Zp

About $424 million in three sessions. SoSoValue’s daily figures show almost all of it went through BlackRock:

The run follows a rough patch. On October 22 the funds lost $635.6 million in a day, their biggest outflow since June, with IBIT and Fidelity’s FBTC each shedding more than $200 million. Through Monday, October was still about $202 million in the red. The two days since have tipped it slightly positive, by roughly $110 million.

The 12 funds now hold $104.9 billion, about 6.4% of all Bitcoin by value, and have taken in $57.6 billion net since they launched in January 2024. IBIT alone holds $66.1 billion.

A hold, but not a quiet one. The Fed’s statement passed 10–2, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack voting for a quarter-point hike. It said the economy is “expanding at a strong pace” and inflation is still too high, and it left the next step to “the accumulation of more information.”

Chair Kevin Warsh gave no hint about December. “I don’t believe in forward guidance, absent exigent circumstances, absent a crisis,” he told reporters, adding that politics “played no role” six days before the midterms. Traders read the dissents as a lean toward tightening. Polymarket’s December market prices a quarter-point hike at 77%, about where it stood before the meeting.

Bitcoin took the decision calmly at first. It traded at $80,860 at 2 p.m. ET and rose 1.1% to $81,788 over the next two hours. The drop came later, during Asian trading, after Samsung’s chip unit missed analysts’ estimates and its shares fell more than 5%, pulling tech stocks lower.

BTC fell to $79,710 by 02:00 UTC, and more than $350 million in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated over 24 hours.

A month of data that will decide whether December’s hike happens. The dates to watch:

November’s reputation as a strong month for Bitcoin rests mostly on two years. On Binance, BTC rose in only three of the last eight Novembers. The big gains, 42.8% in 2020 and 37.2% in 2024, both came right after presidential elections. The two midterm years, 2018 and 2022, ended November down 36.6% and 16.2%.

Bitcoin’s November returns since 2018. Source: Binance

Eight years is a small sample, and both midterm Novembers fell in the middle of bear markets. Options traders aren’t betting on a big move either way. It is testing the area now. BTC trades at $79,899 on Binance, back under its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $80,789, a line it has crossed three times in the past week. The October 24 low of $79,221 is the floor that has held so far.

The one-year view is steadier than the week. The 200-day EMA has climbed from about $72,300 in late August to $76,476, and the 50-day crossed above it on September 12, the first such cross since it fell below in November 2025.

The ETF buyers came back this week, but the Fed left December open and the price is still hostage to tech stocks. For Bitcoin news in the days ahead, the first test is today’s PCE report, and the next is the November 6 jobs data.

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is set for a significant week ahead as its long-awaited cleanup upgrade heads for mainnet activation this week, bringing a wide-ranging collection of fixes and improvements to the blockchain.

The fixCleanup3_4_0 amendment, a collection of fixes for Single Asset Vaults, the Lending Protocol, Automated Market Makers, the permissioned DEX, trust lines, NFTs, MPTs, Escrow, Sponsorship, transaction signing, and permission delegation, is at the center of attention, with validator support putting it on track for a potential November 4 activation, provided the required voting threshold of 80% is sustained.

The earliest activation date is Nov 4, 2026 at 2:46 PM UTC, with just 2 days left according to the xrpscan countdown timer.

Some tokens on the XRP Ledger are supposed to be stored in accounts approved by their issuer; however, developers have found a few ways around that rule.

Issuers of regulated assets, such as stablecoins or tokenized funds, can require approval before anyone holds their tokens, typically to perform identity checks first.

Four proposed code changes would resolve the remaining exceptions. All four are included in a single network upgrade dubbed fixCleanup3_5_0.

These have not been merged into the XRP Ledger's main software yet. Once they are, fixCleanup3_5_0 requires support from more than 80% of the network's trusted validators for two weeks before being activated.

According to Hussein Zangana (Vet), director of community at XRP Ledger Foundation, there is a critical Linux kernel vulnerability on kernels 4.4+, affecting any unpatched Linux server in the world with an open IPv4 TCP port. For XRP Ledger node and validator operators who run RHEL 8/9/10, Debian 12/13, Amazon Linux, and Oracle UEK, a fix has already been shipped; they are simply expected to update and reboot.

For those who run Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky, CentOS Stream, this might not suffice, as they may need to take further steps until a fix is shipped for their distro. They should re-apply the nft rule after a reboot or a flush ruleset reload.

The market is heading into another key macro week. Q3 2026 earnings were a little disappointing.

With costs rising in the AI industry, Amazon saw its free cash flow turn negative at $42.4 billion, causing concern that its huge AI investments may not be providing enough returns to match these valuations. As such, it will be interesting to see how the next set of earnings go.

Apple and Palantir will be reporting on Monday, the 2nd of November.

Notably, the figures are beginning to show just how large the investment gap could be.

According to Bloomberg, this will more than double to roughly $330 billion in FY27, suggesting that AI bubble concerns are more than just short-term market noise. So, with equities under pressure, could this further strengthen Bitcoin’s status as a macro hedge?

Interestingly, this week could offer some clues.

On a macro level, besides earnings reports, The Kobeissi Letter highlights 10 key pieces of data that would provide focus to October’s jobs and inflation figures. This comes at a time when the U.S. midterm elections are looming on the horizon, adding another layer of FUD to an already cautious market.

With the 6.8% drop on the Nasdaq in October and an influx of earnings reports, this could cause a change in market flows. This brings the macro-hedging narrative for Bitcoin back into play.

However, the key question is whether Bitcoin [BTC] can outperform traditional hedges as market uncertainty builds.

Bitcoin’s 2024-2026 setup against gold is gaining attention.

In 2024, Bitcoin outperformed gold by a wide margin. Up 121%, Bitcoin enjoyed a much stronger year than gold (up 27%) due to strong institutional demand and the launch of spot ETFs.

Interestingly, this makes the recent report from The Kobeissi Letter much more interesting given the increasing macro uncertainty that is being seen in the markets.

As shown in the chart below, the largest U.S. physical gold-backed ETF, GLD, saw $1.8 billion in outflows in October, its biggest monthly withdrawal since June. On a year-to-date basis, GLD has lost $3.8 billion, putting it on track for its first annual outflow since 2023.

Meanwhile, investors pulled another $1.5 billion from gold and precious metals funds last week, marking their second weekly outflow in the past seven weeks.

By contrast, Bitcoin ETFs saw a minor $515 million outflow in October.

So technically, GLD recorded nearly 3.5x more outflows than all Bitcoin ETFs combined in October. This is interesting as it comes amid increasing concerns about the AI bubble and pressure on tech stocks, making the coming week particularly important for Bitcoin’s macro hedge narrative.

In this context, Bitcoin could gain more attention as investors reassess traditional safe havens.

Rising AI costs and market uncertainty are putting pressure on equities, bringing Bitcoin’s macro hedge narrative back into focus.

Gold ETFs saw $1.8 billion in outflows in October, compared to just $515 million from Bitcoin ETFs, showing a difference in investor flows.

#5207. MIKA Crypto Crashes 99% After Influencer Posts Her Dev Wallet’s Private Key: Are Celebrity Tokens Back, and Does Anyone Need Them?

An influencer posted her dev wallet key, not the token address, and MIKA crypto crashed in minutes. After LAPTOP, are celebrity tokens back?

Crypto influencer Mika (@mikadontlouz) posted what traders say was her token’s developer wallet private key instead of its contract address. The MIKA crypto token she had just launched crashed about 99% in a single sale minutes later.

For an account with 126,000 followers, that is the equivalent of tweeting your bank PIN with the caption “free yourselves.” Which, as it happens, is roughly what the post said.

Half an hour later she launched again, this time with one wallet holding half the supply. That one is down about 84% from its peak. Bad luck, a botched launch or a tidy exit with a ready-made excuse?

And while we’re asking: after Hunter Biden’s LAPTOP token went the same way in September, are celebrity tokens back, and does anyone actually need them?

Mika just tried to launch a pump coin and instead of tweeting the CA she tweeted the devs wallet private key instead…😭 pic.twitter.com/pjsA0vY7bl

Two launches, two crashes, one afternoon. More or less this is the timeline:

The relaunch now sits at a market cap of about $240,000, with $41,700 of liquidity and $1.65 million traded in 24 hours. The internet, meanwhile, did what it does: DexScreener lists more than a dozen copycats with names like Free Mika King, Jail Mika and Mute Mika.

Maybe. But it was a very specific kind of mistake. Copying a private key instead of a contract address means opening the wallet’s export screen, revealing a string twice as long as the one you meant to share, and pasting it under a caption that starts with “free yourselves.” Plenty of people in crypto have done dumber things. Few have done them with such good copywriting.

Ouhhhh man I'm tired@mikadontlouz "accidentally" posted her private key and "lost $40K"

(was fake.. she put a nonce on the wallet before posting it)

– 400k spawner– dev holds 50%– awful bubblemaps pic.twitter.com/TSsTj8LdFC

— fabiano.sol (@FabianoSolana) October 28, 2026

Whether it was an outsider who copied the key or an existing owner is still unknown, and from the transaction alone the two are hard to tell apart.

To be fair to Mika, none of this proves she meant it. A rushed launch, a clipboard mix-up and a panicked relaunch would leave a similar trail. But a leak that hands the blame for the dump to “whoever copied the key,” a claimed $40,000 loss that may not have happened, and a relaunch where one wallet held half the tokens add up to a lot of coincidences for one afternoon.

DISCOVER: PUMP vs FOMO: Can Signing $40M TRUMP Trader Kimchi Help Pump.fun Win the Launchpad War?

They never really left, they just keep ending the same way. The latest big one came seven weeks ago. Hunter Biden’s LAPTOP token launched on Base on September 9 and jumped to $190.81 two minutes in, on a pool holding about $48,000 of liquidity, then fell to $3.70 within the hour. Biden blamed a market maker and denied his team sold. Bubblemaps found about 80% of LAPTOP traders ended up underwater.

But that is just one in a long list of failed launches by these “celebrities”:

Celebrity tokens, drop from all-time high. Source: CoinGecko

The pattern barely changes. A famous name brings the buyers, insiders or snipers own a large share of the supply, liquidity is thin, and the chart looks like a ski jump. The famous name moves on to the next interview. The people who bought the third green candle don’t.

Short answer: the buyers apparently think so, the charts disagree. A celebrity token has no product, no cash flow and, in most cases, no plan beyond launch day. What it sells is access to a name, and that lasts about as long as the first big holder’s patience.

The tools for spotting trouble keep getting better, too. A Bubblemaps holder map showed the relaunch’s 50% wallet within the hour, and on-chain sleuths had the nonce account screenshotted before the Spaces ended. The second token still traded $1.65 million in 24 hours.

MIKA crypto will probably be forgotten by next week, replaced by the next name with a ticker. If there is a lesson, it’s the oldest one in memecoins: when someone posts “its time to eat,” check who is setting the table.

#5206. XRP Ledger Posts 479% Payment Surge as XRP Heads For Recovery

XRP appears to be starting the new month on a stronger foot as its network activity and price movements over the past day have both turned out to be promising.

Latest onchain data from XRPScan shows a substantial increase in the asset's payment volume on the XRP ledger after closing October with weaker figures.

According to the data, the amount of XRP transferred between accounts on the XRP ledger has surged from around 229 million XRP on October 31 to over 1.33 billion XRP on November 1st.

This marks a substantial increase of over 479% in the metric within the 24-hour period of crossing into November, suggesting that the network is starting the new month with stronger momentum.

While the surge in the XRP payment volume has come at a time when the asset is beginning to show signs of a potential recovery after several weeks of high volatility, it appears that the XRP ledger is also seeing a rebound in its network usage.

Furthermore, the data also suggests that the impact of the recent enormous Binance heist on the network is gradually fading, as activities on the XRP ledger slowed following the incident.

The massive surge in the XRP payment volume could sometimes provide a bullish outlook for XRP's price as it typically signals an increase in the amount of XRP transferred from one account to another, which shows that traders are actively engaging.

While this does not guarantee an instant rally and XRP is yet to show any major price recovery as it is still showing mixed price action, market analysts are hopeful that stronger network activity could rebuild momentum and help the asset restore the gaining streak broken in October.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Shiba Inu (SHIB) exchange reserves have dropped back to about 85.84 trillion tokens in early November, a level that may be healthier for the meme coin's supply. The price, meanwhile, is still under heavy selling pressure.

The latest on-chain data puts SHIB exchange reserves at 85.8432 trillion tokens, up only 0.01% over the past 24 hours. The seven-day chart tells a different story: reserves have fallen noticeably, which suggests a lot of SHIB has left trading platforms.

Lower exchange reserves generally mean fewer tokens are on hand to be sold. When investors pull SHIB into private wallets, there is less supply available to sellers on centralized exchanges. That doesn't guarantee a price recovery, but it can make the supply picture more favorable.

The reserves are currently valued at about $397.45 million, down 1.69% on the day. Exchange netflow is still positive at roughly 10.94 billion SHIB, so short-term selling pressure hasn't gone away.

The supply picture is improving, but the chart is still bearish. On the daily SHIB/USDT chart, the token trades near $0.00000463 after breaking below its ascending support trendline. It is also under several important moving averages, which means sellers still control the broader structure.

Immediate resistance sits around $0.00000500–$0.00000530. The $0.00000440–$0.00000450 region is the next potential support zone.

If demand starts to recover, the drop in exchange-held supply could matter more. For now, the 85 trillion mark is a constructive on-chain sign, not a confirmed bullish reversal. A more convincing case would need continued exchange withdrawals, stronger buying, and a move back above the key resistance levels.

#5203. BNB Crypto Drops 8.7% in an Hour as Binance Loses $6.36 Billion to Hackers, and Futures Traders Turn Short: Can BNB Hold Its 200-Day Average?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour after the Binance hack and is lagging Bitcoin, as shorts pile in. Can BNB hold its 200-day EMA at $692?

BNB crypto fell 8.7% in an hour on Thursday, October 29, from $744.90 to $680, as hackers drained about $6.36 billion from Binance, the exchange behind the token, in the largest crypto theft on record. The bounce since has been the weakest among the big coins. BNB trades at $702, down 6.2% in 24 hours, with a $92.4 billion market cap and 48.7% below its $1,370 record from October 2025. In futures, traders who bet against it are now paying to keep those bets open.

So why is BNB taking the hack harder than Bitcoin, what happened to it after Binance’s last two security scares, and where are the levels that matter?

If a $6.3B security breach can't completely break $BNB, what will?

The market is testing @BNBCHAIN resilience right now.

Historically, moments of maximum fear can create the best opportunities.

DISCOVER: Meme coin supercycle: Top performers this week

Because it is the coin most tied to Binance itself, and futures traders are now betting on that link. From the 20:00 UTC price on Thursday, BNB is still down 5.6%, more than Bitcoin, Ether, Solana, XRP or Dogecoin.

Large-cap coins since the Binance hack. Source: Binance

The hack itself didn’t touch BNB Chain. TRM Labs’ breakdown lists ten blockchains the attacker drained Binance wallets on, from Ethereum to Polygon, and BNB Chain isn’t among them. What traders are pricing is the exchange: BNB is Binance’s token, so a hit to Binance reads as a hit to BNB.

“The Binance exploit has intensified market-wide selling, with BNB facing the greatest exposure,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John said. Rick Maeda of Laevitas saw it the other way, calling the drop “quite modest for possibly the largest exchange theft ever.”

The futures market sides with the bears. On OKX:

Put together, that reads as many small accounts buying the dip and fewer, larger traders shorting it. If BNB bounces, those shorts are fuel for a squeeze. If it breaks lower, the crowded longs are.

It fell further at first, then recovered within a month both times. Binance has been here twice before:

This time BNB is 8.7% under its pre-hack price at its worst so far. If it follows either path, there could be another leg down before any recovery.

The comparison traders keep reaching for is FTT, the FTX token that lost almost all its value when the exchange collapsed in November 2022. The difference is the balance sheet. FTX had spent customer money and couldn’t pay it back. Binance says it will cover all losses from this hack, and Tether, Circle and others froze about $2.7 billion of the stolen funds within hours.

Traders haven’t fully relaxed, though. Binance hasn’t said how it will fund the payout, and withdrawals stay shut until the reopening it expects within 48 hours of its Friday morning update.

EXPLORE: CZ Tells Crypto Users to Be “Extra Careful” Online as PHP Vulnerabilities Hit the Code Behind 70% of Websites: Can a Hacked Site Drain Your Wallet?

It is holding by a thin margin. BNB closed Thursday at $698.46, just above its 200-day exponential moving average (EMA) at $692.46, after the hack-hour wick to $680 dipped below it. The 50-day EMA at $733.06 is now overhead.

The four-month chart puts BNB back where it was in late August. It traded between $674.60 and $726 for two weeks before breaking out in early September and running to $809.99 on October 5. Thursday’s drop erased that whole move.

For BNB crypto, the next 48 hours carry more weight than any chart line. A smooth reopening of Binance withdrawals would leave the shorts on the wrong side of a crowded trade. A delay, or any sign Binance is selling BNB to pay for the hack, would put $674.60 in play.

#5202. Binance net outflows cross $3.64B after withdrawals restart – Can user confidence return?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

On Sunday, the 1st of November, at 06:00 UTC, Binance resumed withdrawals, allowing users to withdraw their assets. Immediately upon opening for withdrawals again, there was an increase in the volume of withdrawal transactions.

Within the first two hours of withdrawals reopening, $733 million was withdrawn before gradually declining as the initial rush eased. However, a high volume of withdrawals continued to be initiated throughout the day.

This indicated users were continuing to withdraw their assets from the exchange even though they can do so.

As of 15:30 UTC, withdrawals totaled $4.649 billion, and deposits totaled $1.01 billion, thus resulting in a net withdrawal amount of $3.638 billion. This represents 2.1% of Binance’s stated $171 billion in assets.

Although the net outflow indicates a large number of post-resumption withdrawals were made from the exchange, it may not indicate a loss of confidence. The fact that deposits continue to occur, along with decreasing withdrawal rates, suggests that trading activity appears to be normalizing.

However, if a large volume of additional withdrawals are made, it will decrease the exchange’s reserve levels and liquidity.

Soon after the withdrawals began, some assets experienced outflows in larger volumes. Notably, Tether [USDT] led with the most outflows, with 1.96 billion tokens leaving the exchange.

USD Coin [USDC] trailed closely by 557.65 million tokens. Still, during this time, Binance saw 19,569 Bitcoins [BTC] worth approximately $1.53 billion leave the exchange. Meanwhile, while Ethereum [ETH] outflows totalled 154,147 ETH, valued near $360 million.

This distribution shows that users moved both stablecoins and major cryptocurrencies rather than concentrating on one asset.

Given that many users withdrew both types of assets, many seem to want to maximize their liquidity and ease transferability. Simultaneously, Bitcoin and ETH outflows further reduced assets held on Binance

Continued removals could negatively affect exchanges‘ reserves and delay the end of the examination into the security measures taken by Binance.

Now, instead of focusing solely on the breach itself, Binance is facing pressure to determine what portion of the stolen funds cannot be recovered. Both Tether and Circle have issued freezes on approximately $2.7-$3 billion in stablecoins.

This severely limits attackers’ ability to withdraw any part of the funds. Binance claims that through company funds and SAFU reserve accounts, they have been able to recover over 90% of the impacted assets.

Nonetheless, most of the remaining exposure is comprised of Bitcoin and ETH. These assets are far more difficult to freeze since they are currently controlled by attackers.

Furthermore, independent verification of the amounts reported by Binance regarding recovery is extremely important. Until transaction records clarify the outstanding balance, confidence will depend on evidence rather than reported progress.

Binance recorded $3.64 billion in net outflows after reopening withdrawals following the hack.

Binance recovered over 90% of stolen assets, but the remaining losses threaten user confidence.

Kicking off that campaign with Stellar’s XLM Network back in 2021, The original U.S. OnChain US Government Money Fund (FOBXX / BENJI) remains heavily concentrated there.

The intricacies of how Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) works has caught the attention of Sandy Kaul, the firm’s Head of Innovation. In a recent interview, Ms. Kaul was explaining how the asset manager now calculates interest on their own tokenized money market fund (MMF) with precision as the fund expanded to other DLTs.

Currently, Stellar’s (XLM) RWA usage is hitting unprecedented peaks, but the toll on Stellar Lumen’s native token due to the bearish market conditions seems to overshadow the bearish tone imposed from the rising niche. With Franklin Templeton managing beyond $650 million in assets on Stellar now, it’s clear that XLM Network remains the top destination.

An unknown investor has built a position in Zcash (ZEC) worth about $14 million, splitting the capital between the spot market and the decentralized derivatives exchange Hyperliquid. The purchases came amid preparations for the Network Upgrade 7 (NU7) hard fork: on November 5, it is set to speed up block processing threefold.

Judging by on-chain data, the address t1JJnA linked to the investor first bought 3,052 ZEC (about $3.8 million) on the spot market at an average price of $1,250. Then, on Hyperliquid, it opened a 2x leveraged long on 8,000 ZEC worth $10.16 million in two different wallets.

So far, 3,000 ZEC of this position can be verified, with an average entry price of $1,353.83.

In late October, ZEC pulled back to the $1,220–$1,280 range, and the derivatives position went into the red. At its peak, the paper loss exceeded $1.8 million; it now stands at $249,388.

But liquidation will only occur if the price falls to $647.67, which is nearly half of current levels. The investor is clearly betting on long-term growth rather than a quick rebound.

The main argument is the NU7 hard fork, whose final tests the developers completed on the testnet in October. The ZIP-218 update will cut block time from 75 to 25 seconds: the network’s throughput will triple, while the issuance schedule will remain the same.

Along with the hard fork, the Network Sustainability Mechanism (a reserve fee fund for miners) will go live, and the outdated Sprout pool will be shut down in favor of the shielded Orchard architecture.

Throughout 2026, each new Zcash low came in higher than the previous one. An ascending triangle has formed on the chart, and time after time the price runs into resistance at $1,396. Traders on the derivatives market have split into two camps.

Some expect a sharp upside breakout amid inflows into the Grayscale Zcash Trust. Others fear that right after the upgrade activates on November 5, the “buy the rumor, sell the news” principle will kick in.

#5199. Binance Hacker Sits on $1.4 Billion in Bitcoin, Triple a Week of ETF Buying, as Route 2 FI Buys the Dip

Bitcoin news: the Binance hacker holds $1.4B in BTC, 3x this week’s ETF inflows. Will Binance’s buyback help, and can BTC hold $76,500?

Bitcoin news on Friday turned to a warning from trader Route 2 FI, who said the Binance hacker’s $1.4 billion in BTC is more than three times what spot ETFs bought all week, a potential seller hanging over Bitcoin at $77,300.

Arkham’s entity page shows the Binance hacker holding 18,270 BTC worth $1.42 billion and 488,364 ETH worth $1.09 billion across 73 addresses. US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million from Monday to Thursday.

Route 2 FI still likes the setup enough to take a position. The trader expects Binance to recover fully but thinks the hack will push more people toward decentralized exchanges.

Binance would need a couple of months to fill this hole, unless they use other shady tactics to get whole faster.

The hacker has $BTC worth $1.4b and $ETH worth $1b ready to sell. For $BTC, that's more than 3x the $450M that spot ETFs bought all week.

— Route 2 FI (@Route2FI) October 30, 2026

DISCOVER: Bitcoin Holds $79,200 Before the Fed, Coinbase Earnings and a $10.9B Expiry: Which Way Next?

Route 2 FI’s math holds up. Arkham’s Binance Hacker entity shows 18,270 BTC, worth $1.42 billion at Friday’s prices. SoSoValue figures show US spot Bitcoin ETFs took in about $440.7 million across four straight days of inflows from October 26 to 29. That makes the hacker’s Bitcoin about 3.2 times a week of ETF demand.

Binance hacker holdings on October 30, 2026 vs spot Bitcoin ETF inflows for October 26 to 29. Sources: Arkham, SoSoValue.

The hacker hasn’t sold any of the Bitcoin yet. The selling so far has been in smaller tokens: Lookonchain tracked the attacker dumping UNI, PEPE, ENA, LINK and others for 70,480 ETH, worth about $158 million.

On the other side, Binance is already buying. The exchange told CoinDesk it has set aside more than $6.34 billion to cover the losses, $5 billion of it already held in the same tokens the attackers took, and is buying the rest on exchanges and over the counter. About $3 billion of the stolen funds is frozen and doesn’t need replacing.

“Binance’s SAFU fund and Binance’s holdings include a large amount of assets such as BTC and ETH. We are currently buying, through OTC and on-exchange, all the stolen altcoins in fully matching amounts.”

That matters for Bitcoin. If Binance already holds enough BTC to cover customers, its buying lands mostly on altcoins, which leaves the hacker’s 18,270 BTC as a seller without a matching buyer.

Route 2 FI pointed to the Bybit hack as the template. Attackers took about $1.4 billion in ether from Bybit on February 21, 2025, and the exchange replaced it within days through loans, deposits and market purchases.

The buyback gave prices only a short lift. Measured from the February 20, 2025 close on Binance:

Ethereum bounced while Bybit bought, then lost more than a third of its value within three weeks. The broader market sold off over that stretch for reasons beyond the hack, so the table shows that buyback demand fades fast. It doesn’t show that the hack caused the slide.

Route 2 FI also argued that the hack, coming a year after the October 10, 2025 crash, gives traders another reason to keep less money on centralized exchanges. Binance paid out more than $283 million in compensation after that crash, when some assets lost their pegs on its platform.

The trader cited the jump in Hyperliquid’s HYPE token as proof. The timing doesn’t fit, though. HYPE rose from $79.38 to a $97.09 high between 10:00 and 16:00 UTC on Thursday, after ICE and Trade.xyz announced plans for a regulated US perpetuals venue on Hyperliquid. That was about ten hours before the Binance drain began at 20:04 UTC.

After the hack, HYPE fell to $88.55 and trades at $90.83.

EXPLORE: Bitcoin Whale Sends $35M to Coinbase at a $15M Loss as October Turns Red: What Moves BTC Next?

The setup Route 2 FI is buying is easy to see on the daily chart since early August. Bitcoin’s $76,500 low on Friday stopped $35 above its 200-day EMA at $76,465, a line it has closed above every day since the late-August breakout. BTC trades at $77,326, down 3.5% in 24 hours.

August 2 to October 30, 2026: BTCUSDT 1D chart. Source: TradingView

The last time Bitcoin tested the 200-day line, in mid-September, it held at $74,968 and climbed to $87,395 within a week. A trader buying here has a clear line to be wrong at.

For Bitcoin news over the coming week, two things decide which row plays out: whether Binance reopens withdrawals on schedule, and whether the hacker’s Bitcoin starts to move.

#5196. Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Home » Cardano (ADA) » Cardano Foundation Joins Swiss CMTA. ADA Tests $0.20

Cardano Foundation just opened the path for multi-billion tokenized shares on the mainstream Layer-1 network.

The Cardano Foundation has joined Switzerland’s Capital Markets and Technology Association, and the group has recognized Cardano’s CIP-0113 programmable token standard as equivalent to its own CMTAT framework for certifying tokenized shares.

The move advances regulated securities tokenization on the network at the same time ADA trades in a clear bearish structure and tests the $0.182 area.

The Foundation announced membership in CMTA on October 29. CMTA is the Swiss industry association that develops practical standards for issuing and managing securities on distributed ledgers.

Following the mainnet launch of CIP-0113 earlier in the month, CMTA’s Expert Committee treated a reviewed Cardano implementation of the standard as technically equivalent to CMTAT for equity securities.

NEW: Cardano Foundation joins CMTA, the Swiss entity "setting the standard for tokenized capital markets," alongside members including UBS, with $7T in AUM. CMTA has recognized $ADA's CIP-113 as "equivalent to the CMTAT—meaning issuers can use it to tokenize certifiable shares." pic.twitter.com/iqmz811b4U

Issuers that meet the deployment conditions can therefore use it to tokenize shares that are eligible for CMTA’s certification process.

CIP-0113 went live on Cardano’s (ADA) mainnet on October 7 without a hard fork. It lets issuers attach compliance rules.

KYC and AML checks, sanctions screening, freeze and seize powers, and transfer restrictions, directly to native Cardano tokens. The ledger enforces those rules on every transfer, mint, or burn.

The blokchain recognition is limited to tokenized shares (equity), does not extend to tokenized debt or Cardano’s base-layer infrastructure, and still requires each issuance to satisfy Swiss legal and technical checks.

Shortly after launch, Veridian, a digital-identity company spun out from the Foundation, tokenized its own shares as ledger-based securities under Switzerland’s DLT Act using the standard, becoming the first publicly identified issuer to do so.

While the institutional groundwork advances, ADA’s chart tells a different short-term story. On the 4-hour timeframe the token continues a downtrend of lower highs and lower lows. It has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is testing the $0.182 area.

$ADA / USDT – 4HCardano continues trading in a strong bearish downtrend with lower highs and lower lows 👀📉ADA has slipped below the $0.20 support zone and is now testing $0.182. Buyers need to step in quickly to prevent further downside.🎯 Bullish recovery target: $0.2188… pic.twitter.com/VVA9FFVh1W

A reclaim of $0.20 is widely viewed as the first requirement for any shift in near-term sentiment, with resistance levels clustered around 0.2004–0.2188.

Until that reclaim occurs, bears remain in control and further downside remains possible if buyers fail to defend the current zone.

The CMTA membership and CIP-0113 equivalence give Cardano a clearer route into regulated tokenized capital markets in Switzerland, where ledger-based securities already have a defined legal framework. MSB Intel says the opportunities are in the trillions.

The Cardano Foundation has joined CMTA, the Swiss body that sets tokenized securities standards, whose members include UBS, Pictet and Lombard Odier.UBS alone has $7.328T in invested assets.@Cardano pic.twitter.com/Vb4bVAac0X

No doubt, this is the kind of standard work that makes real-world assets (RWAs) practical rather than purely experimental.

At the same time, the token’s price continues to reflect broader market weakness, with ADA trading near $0.19 and still well below prior cycle levels. For now the institutional plumbing is moving forward even as the chart remains under pressure.

October was a reality check for AI crypto as AI-driven FUD hit risk sentiment.

Concerns around high AI spending, higher indebtedness, and the uncertainty of returns have led to a sell-off in AI-related stocks spilling into cryptocurrency. The biggest macro overhang came from late-October earnings reports, which added pressure across U.S. equities.

As can be seen below, the top AI stock (Nvidia) lost 10%+ in October, marking its sharpest monthly decline since the 2025 crash. This demonstrates just how much capital flow is influencing AI sentiment right now.

From a technical standpoint, the answer looks straightforward.

The largest AI-associated crypto by market cap, NEAR Protocol [NEAR], fell over 16% during the same time-frame. It lost over $200 million in market cap. This wiped out almost half of the 178% rally seen in September, which was one of its best months in recent months.

This shows how AI-induced FUD is starting to seep into the market, and NEAR is already showing some signs of losing momentum.

However, it is also another major macro week for crypto, with some major cap earnings in focus (Apple). The main question will be whether there is a rebound in AI stocks during the month of November or if the selloff continues, which will dictate what happens to AI-linked cryptos next.

October was a reality check for the AI trade.

Adding to the pressure was the news that earnings were not as impressive as hoped for both Intel and Amazon. On the 30th of October, the Nasdaq fell by 2.86%, with Nvidia falling by 4.2% and AMD falling by 10.9%.

Overall, the Nasdaq 100 fell by over 5.8% in October, putting over $2 trillion at risk.

This weakness also spilled into AI crypto. According to CoinPaprika data, the sector’s total market cap fell from $16.32 billion on the 3rd of October to $13.72 billion on the 31st of October, wiping out roughly $2.6 billion, or 16%, during the month.

This followed a dramatic drop from the impressive 54% rally seen in September, which far outpaced the 24% increase seen by the wider crypto market.

In essence, October’s FUD spilled over into AI crypto, triggering a sharp cooldown in sector valuations.

Looking ahead to macro week, Apple earnings, U.S. midterm elections, and key U.S. economic data out of October could all provide the next trigger point in terms of risks.

It means that if Apple has strong earnings, then it will help solidify the AI trade; however, if it is more disappointing, then the market could see continued weakness across the AI crypto space.

AI crypto lost 16% of its market cap as AI fears hit stocks and crypto.

November outlook: Apple earnings, U.S. elections, and economic data could decide whether AI crypto recovers or falls further.

Binance has published its latest Proof of Reserves report as of October 31, 2026. Judging by it, client funds are still fully backed — despite the largest hack in crypto history at the end of the month. Coverage for XRP is 100.99%, and for the Ripple USD (RLUSD) stablecoin, 100.83%.

A comparison of balances as of October 1 and October 31 shows how the exchange's liabilities and reserves changed after the October 29 attack: hackers then withdrew about $6.3 billion from its wallets across ten blockchains.

Immediately after the attack, Binance suspended withdrawals and deposits, so the growth of balances in Ripple assets occurred before the hack. October results:

The main thing in the report is something else: Binance confirmed full coverage of the ten most traded assets, including BTC, ETH, USDT, BNB and SOL — and did so just two days after the hack.

About $3 billion of the stolen funds was quickly frozen directly on the blockchains with the help of partners, including Tether, Circle and Ripple. To cover the losses and return reserves to 1:1, Binance allocated more than $6.34 billion of its own capital. This reserve included the SAFU fund, the Binance Futures insurance fund and retained earnings.

The remaining 5% of losses are in low-liquidity tokens: they are being quietly bought back through over-the-counter (OTC) desks so as not to crash spot prices.

Each client can verify their own balance: the report is built on Merkle trees and zero-knowledge proofs (zk-SNARKs). For the market, this case sets a new bar: an exchange is no longer judged by whether it gets hacked, but by how quickly it stops an attack and whether it has enough of its own money to plug the hole.

#5192. Sui’s 40M TPS Demo Comes With an Off-Chain Caveat

Home » Trendsetter News » Sui’s 40M TPS Demo Comes With an Off-Chain Caveat

Sui’s 40M TPS demonstration highlights blockchain’s push for speed, but its off-chain design raises questions about the actual figures.

Sui reached more than 40 million transactions per second in a demonstration highlighted by crypto commentator Linda, but those transactions did not run directly through its mainnet.

The demonstration, which she says took place at Sui Base Camp during Token2049 in early October, used “tunnels” to process activity off-chain before settling results on-chain. That makes it a different proposition from sustained mainnet throughput.

Linda connects the test to Sui chain push into AI-agent infrastructure. A Sui chain co-founder’s clip featured in the video describes plans for agent coordination, payments and auditable activity, alongside collaboration with Google.

The strategic ambition is clear; the demonstration alone does not establish production demand.

She describes potential private versions of Ethereum applications such as Uniswap and Aave, plus private swaps accessible through existing Solana wallets.

She also reports that Midnight has passed one million mainnet transactions and that daily transactions increased nearly 400-fold in a month.

The YouTube video does not supply the starting daily transaction count, limiting what that growth multiple says about sustained adoption.

#5186. HashPack Adds HBAR Tokenized Stock Without LP Reliance

Home » Trendsetter News » HashPack Adds HBAR Tokenized Stock Without LP Reliance

HashPack users can now access tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX using HBAR or Hedera’s wrapped USDC version.

HashPack users can now buy tokenized stocks and ETFs through SODAX without relying on liquidity pools on Hedera, according to CEO and co-founder May. Speaking with the host about the wallet’s latest upgrades, she described an integration that lets users pay with HBAR or Hedera USDC while accessing liquidity outside the network.

That distinction matters for larger trades. Assets traded through shallow pools can suffer significant price slippage; May said the SODAX integration avoids depending on locally supplied liquidity to execute purchases.

According to May, buyers receive an HTS token representing a Robinhood stock token issued on Robinhood Chain. She said SODAX maintains the one-to-one relationship, giving users exposure to the underlying asset’s price without requiring another wallet or a manual move to another blockchain.

“You’re not relying on liquidity that exists on the network,” she said. Previously, most assets available to trade through HashPack depended on SaucerSwap pools, apart from token-launch platforms that subsequently created pools there.

May also described dividends as being reinvested into the same stock rather than distributed as cash, qualifying that explanation with “as far as I know.”

The interview did not establish the products’ legal ownership rights, redemption terms or geographic restrictions; details investors would need before treating them as interchangeable with brokerage-held shares.

She sees potential for lending and borrowing against tokenized stocks, although the discussion did not establish that those functions are available inside HashPack.

The stock integration accompanies HashPack’s “Portfolio” redesign, which adds a customizable homepage and bottom-opening navigation dock. May said most users access the wallet on mobile, and its growing collection of swaps, staking options and NFT integrations had made features harder to find.

Enterprise integrations remain a slower prospect. HashPack has ongoing discussions, May said, but nothing particularly exciting to flag for the short term; she suggested developments could emerge over 12 to 24 months.

#5185. BTCPay Server Tells Merchants to Shut Down After Attackers Sweep Hot Wallets: Are Payments Still Safe?

Bitcoin news: BTCPay Server told merchants to go offline after attackers swept hot wallets on 2.4.1 or older. Here is who is exposed.

In today’s Bitcoin news, BTCPay Server, the free open-source payment processor many Bitcoin merchants run themselves, told every operator to shut down their instance after reports that attackers were sweeping the hot wallets on merchant servers. Less than six hours later, the culprit was old software.

At 04:07 UTC on Monday, the project said its investigation had found an attack vector aimed at servers running version 2.4.1, released on July 23, or older. It has “no credible reports” of drains on the current 2.4.7. BTCPay has not said how much was stolen or how many stores were hit.

That makes this a different kind of Bitcoin news from last week’s Binance hack. No exchange was breached. Merchants who run their own payment stack, the people self-custody is meant to protect, were the target.

So who was exposed, and what should store owners do now?

Unauthorized attackers are reportedly draining hot wallets on @BtcpayServer instances.

Users running BTCPay Server instances are advised to shut them down immediately. pic.twitter.com/H7mXfJLLcD

— Lookonchain (@lookonchain) November 2, 2026

Market Intelligence: Crypto Security Analyst Recommends Best Anonymous Crypto Wallets

An attacker logged in as admin on older servers and emptied the hot wallets. BTCPay Server raised the alarm at 22:25 UTC on Sunday and asked operators to run its shutdown script “until we complete the investigation.”

Two hours later, founder Nicolas Dorier said the project’s own public servers on 2.4.7 were not attacked. “The attacker managed to log in as admin on those instance, we are still trying to figure out how,” he wrote.

📢 Our incident response investigation identified an attack vector targeting instances running versions 2.4.1 (Jul 23, 2026) or older.

We have no credible reports of hot wallet drains for users running the latest 2.4.7 release. We again urge everyone to keep their BTCPay Server… pic.twitter.com/gYxK4Bb7fc

— BTCPay Server (@BtcpayServer) November 2, 2026

A hot wallet keeps its signing keys on the server itself, so it can pay out refunds and payouts automatically. Anyone with admin rights on that server can send the coins too.

Hosting providers moved fast. BTCPay thanked LunaNode and others for shutting down older hosted instances on their own, so some merchants may find their store offline on Monday.

The version history is the story. 2.4.1 shipped on July 23. Two weeks later, 2.4.2 fixed a critical flaw the team said was “being actively exploited,” and five more releases followed, ending with Thursday’s 2.4.7, which fixed 85 findings from an AI security scan Anthropic ran for the project.

Whether this is the same hole as August’s is still open. Dorier said a blog post with more detail is coming.

Only if it still runs 2.4.1 or older, on what the project knows so far. “For those who already updated at least once since the release of 2.4.2, there is no reason to panic,” Dorier wrote at 04:10 UTC.

The reported drains all hit hot wallets. Stores that receive into a watch-only wallet keep their signing keys off the server altogether.

#5183. Animoca Announces ADGM Fund-Management Permission for Institutional Expansion

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Animoca Brands has added a fund-management authorization in Abu Dhabi to its institutional business. The company announced on November 2 that Animoca Asset Management (AD) Limited had received Financial Services Permission from ADGM’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority to manage collective investment funds in or from the financial centre.

The company announcement follows an earlier effective date: the ADGM register dates permission 250097 to October 13, 2026. It prohibits dealing with retail clients and holding or controlling client assets, defining a narrower scope than a general licence to provide every crypto service.

A professionally managed fund can bring several decisions into one structure: the investment mandate, who has discretion over transactions, how assets are valued and what investors receive in return for contributing capital. That can make a digital-asset strategy easier to assess than a collection of direct token purchases.

It also creates a clearer place to ask difficult questions. An investor can examine the manager’s authority, the legal entity responsible for the assets and the process for calculating performance. Those questions remain important whether a portfolio holds tokens, equity in blockchain companies or another form of exposure.

For Animoca, the potential commercial advantage is being able to meet an allocator through a regulated investment-management structure. Permission does not itself supply investor demand, a track record for a new strategy or a pool of committed money.

The group’s presence elsewhere in the UAE offers relevant context without changing the meaning of this approval. Dubai’s VARA public register separately lists Animoca Brands Middle East Advisory FZCO for broker-dealer and management and investment services, with institutional and qualified-investor conditions.

The entities and regulators should not be collapsed into a single blanket licence. A client dealing with an investment manager needs to know which company signs the agreement, what service it provides and which permissions apply to that relationship.

This becomes particularly relevant when a group operates across investments, advisory work, technology and token-related services. A recognizable brand can span several businesses whose responsibilities differ. Documentation needs to follow the actual service, rather than relying on the reputation of the parent.

An investor with a wide network of technology businesses may have access to early projects, founders and commercial information that an outside allocator cannot easily obtain. That can be useful when evaluating young markets where conventional financial histories are limited.

The same proximity creates questions about potential conflicts. A fund might encounter opportunities involving companies in which a related business already has an interest. Investors would reasonably want to understand how such situations are identified, reviewed and disclosed, without assuming from the authorization alone that any particular transaction is planned.

Valuation is another practical issue. A liquid token, a venture investment and a contractual right to future revenue can behave very differently when markets weaken. Combining them in a strategy requires a coherent explanation of liquidity and how often investors can withdraw.

The next meaningful disclosures would concern named funds, their objectives, eligible investors, custody arrangements, fees and redemption terms. Those details turn a broad institutional ambition into something a prospective allocator can compare with other options.

Capital raised is also different from assets already invested. A fund can secure commitments before deploying them, and a product can launch without immediately reaching material scale. Keeping those stages separate makes progress easier to measure.

For now, Animoca has reported an additional regulated capability in a market central to its regional expansion. The authorization strengthens the framework through which the group can pursue institutional business; the quality of the investment products built within that framework will determine the longer-term outcome.

#5182. Solana Officially Scores 1,000 Days Without Outage

The Solana network has hit a significant milestone in its quest to overcome its early hurdles, successfully going 1,000 days without a network-wide outage.

This feat stands in stark contrast to Solana's past, when the blockchain experienced some notable network disruptions. One of the more significant outages occurred in September 2021, when a spike in bot traffic from Grape Protocol IDO transactions led to a surge in transactions that overwhelmed validators and hindered consensus, resulting in a roughly 17-hour network outage.

The Solana network experienced similar problems in April 2022, with a large traffic spike due to an NFT mint that led to a roughly 7-hour outage. Another outage happened in June 2022, when a bug involving durable nonce transactions caused block production to stop for roughly 4.5 hours. Finally, in September 2022, the network experienced a fork due to a bug in the consensus layer, which led to a halt in block production lasting over 6 hours.

The final major outage occurred back in February 2023, when abnormal block forwarding overwhelmed Solana's Turbine block propagation system, leaving validators stuck in a vote-only state and leading to a coordinated restart. This would prove to be a monumental event for Solana in terms of its engineering progress.

Solana has seen a string of updates and engineering innovations by its developers in an effort to improve the network's ability to avoid the failures that had plagued it in the past. Some of these features include stake-weighted quality of service to better prioritize traffic from staked validators. The network also saw networking innovations such as QUIC that provide more flexibility in dealing with spam and congestion. There have also been updates to deduplication logic following the February 2023 outage. Additionally, the network has seen innovations such as a local fee market and other scheduling improvements to discourage users and bots from spamming the network with duplicate transactions.

Recently, Solana has emphasized that network resilience should be taken seriously. In a September 2026 update, the project shared that the network has seen 100% uptime since February 2024 and has continued to handle large amounts of traffic. It also highlighted a major infrastructure provider experiencing a routing failure in August 2026 that caused validators representing nearly 29% of the network's stake to go offline, but this did not result in a halt in block production. The project uses this as an example of increased fault tolerance.

For Solana, this 1,000-day milestone is not just a success in terms of network uptime. It's a statement and a demonstration to the world that a network once mocked for outages can now support serious financial and on-chain use cases.

#5181. 5 Best AI Crypto Trading Bots

Home » Cryptopedia » 5 Best AI Crypto Trading Bots

Compare five AI crypto trading bots by automation features, strategy tools, supported exchanges, ease of use, and key limitations.

AI crypto trading bots help traders automate strategies, analyze market data, and manage trade execution without monitoring charts around the clock. However, not every crypto trading bot marketed as AI-powered uses artificial intelligence to make trading decisions. Some platforms rely primarily on predefined rules, while others use AI to build strategies, interpret market conditions, or configure automated trading systems.

The best AI crypto trading bot depends on what you need: strategy automation, AI-assisted decision-making, beginner-friendly controls, or trading across multiple exchanges. This guide compares five platforms based on their available features, intended use cases, and practical limitations.

We looked at each platform’s automation features, strategy tools, backtesting options, supported exchanges, ease of use, pricing, and risk-management features. We also checked the information against each platform’s official website. Our picks are based on the features each bot offers and who it may suit best, rather than independently tested trading results. Keep in mind that features, fees, and exchange support can change over time.

3Commas is a crypto trading platform that combines automated bots with tools for managing and executing trades. It is widely used for multi-exchange order execution and parameter-driven  3Commas AI Trading Bot setups.

Its features include Dollar-Cost Averaging (DCA) bots, grid bots, signal-based trading, and SmartTrade order management.

The platform also offers an AI trading assistant that lets users describe a strategy in natural language. According to 3Commas, the assistant can configure a bot, run a backtest using historical market data, and prepare the strategy for launch.

Limitation: Bot capacity on the entry plan is small, and higher limits require Pro or Expert. Backtests also cannot fully reproduce future market conditions, slippage, liquidity constraints, or unexpected volatility.

3Commas is worth considering for traders who want to automate established trading strategies while retaining control over entry conditions, position sizing, and exits. It is particularly relevant to users who already understand concepts such as DCA, grid trading, and technical indicators.

Cryptohopper is a cloud-based engine that combines automated crypto trading with strategy-building, backtesting, and AI-assisted tools.

Its AI Strategy Designer helps traders choose strategies, signal providers, and TradingView alerts based on current market conditions. However, access depends on the subscription plan, so it’s worth checking the requirements before signing up.

Cryptohopper also has Cryptohopper.AI, a separate tool that lets users create trading bots and other trading tools simply by describing what they want in plain language. Although both use AI, they serve different purposes and shouldn’t be confused with each other.

Limitation: Access to certain AI features depends on the product and subscription tier. AI-generated strategies still require testing and monitoring before live deployment.

Cryptohopper trading bot suits traders who want to experiment with different strategies and automate their selection or execution. It is also relevant to users interested in building customized crypto trading tools without writing all the code themselves.

Pionex is a cryptocurrency exchange with AI trading bots built directly into its platform. Unlike third-party automation services that require users to connect exchange accounts, Pionex integrates bot functionality into the exchange itself.

Pionex offers 16 bots, including Grid Trading, Infinity Grid, Trailing Buy/Sell, Rebalancing, and Spot-Futures Arbitrage bots. The options also include PionexGPT, an AI-related feature that allows users to write custom trading strategies using natural language prompts.

Limitations:  Funds are held on the Pionex exchange rather than on an exchange you already use, so the AI trading bots cannot be applied to other exchanges.

Pionex is a good option for beginners who want to try automated trading without paying for a separate bot service or connecting to another exchange. It can also be useful for experienced traders who prefer to manage everything on one platform.

Coinrule focuses on rule-based crypto trading automation. Users can create strategies by setting simple rules rather than building a trading system entirely from scratch.

With features like Coinrule AI Cloud, users can also use plain language to create trading strategies, get help setting them up, test them against historical data, and connect with compatible AI assistants.

Limitation: Rule-based automation follows its configured conditions; it does not inherently understand market context or predict future prices. It doesn’t provide the level of mathematical detail and precise order book analysis that professional institutional traders need.

Coinrule is suitable for traders who know what conditions they want to trade but do not want to write the underlying code. It is also useful for users who want to test systematic strategies before connecting them to live trading.

Bitsgap is a crypto trading platform that brings everything together in one place, including automated crypto AI trading bots, portfolio management, analytics, and exchange connections. It offers different trading bots, such as Grid and DCA, to help users automate their strategies. Its AI Assistant also helps users configure their trading setups.

With support for multiple crypto exchanges, Bitsgap lets users manage their trading activities through a single interface.

Limitation: Futures bots are not available on the Basic plan.Exchange support and available features vary.

Bitsgap is a good option for traders who use multiple exchanges and want to manage their trading bots in one place. Its automation tools and analytics also make it easier to track strategies and monitor performance.

The best AI crypto trading bot is the one whose capabilities match your trading approach, not necessarily the one with the most AI features.

Before choosing a platform, compare these factors:

AI crypto trading bots can automate execution and reduce the need for constant manual monitoring, but profitability is never guaranteed. Results depend on strategy design, market conditions, execution costs, liquidity, and risk management.

Historical backtests are useful for evaluating a strategy, but they do not establish that it will perform similarly in live markets. Traders should test bots in simulation where possible, start with limited exposure, and monitor performance after deployment.

An AI label alone is not evidence of a trading advantage. Before selecting a bot, establish what the AI actually does, how trades are triggered, and how losses are managed.

The answer depends on the use case. Pionex requires no API setup or subscription, 3Commas builds bots from plain-English prompts, Bitsgap covers 17+ exchanges, and Cryptohopper offers a strategy marketplace.

No profitability can be assumed. Results depend on settings, fees, and market conditions, and losses are possible.

It depends on the platform. 3Commas states it is non-custodial and connects through APIs, while Pionex operates as an exchange where funds are deposited.

#5180. Anchorpoint Plans Native HKDAP on Solana as Hong Kong Dollar Access Expands

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Hong Kong dollar stablecoin issuer Anchorpoint plans to bring HKDAP to Solana through a collaboration announced on October 30. The proposed expansion would give the token a native route into another blockchain ecosystem, with payments and tokenized-asset transactions among the intended uses.

Anchorpoint’s official release describes planned native minting and redemption. It does not announce that public Solana issuance or unrestricted retail access has already begun.

A stablecoin tied to the Hong Kong dollar could be useful when the payment, investment or accounting obligation is denominated in that currency. Holding a dollar token referenced to a different currency can add a conversion step and expose the user to exchange-rate movements before the final payment is made.

Placing the instrument on a network already used by a potential customer changes the access problem. A wallet or application would not necessarily need to send users to another chain before they could settle a Hong Kong dollar obligation.

The business case depends on actual demand for that currency within the ecosystem. A new network listing does not create a payment corridor by itself. Merchants, investment platforms and counterparties still need reasons to receive the token and dependable ways to use or redeem it.

A native token is issued on the destination network under the issuer’s arrangements. A bridged representation adds a mechanism linking an asset in one location to a representation elsewhere. Those architectures place responsibility for transfers and backing in different places.

For a treasury team, that distinction affects reconciliation. The team needs to establish what it owns, which entity owes redemption and how to identify the genuine asset. A familiar ticker displayed in a wallet is insufficient evidence of any of those points.

The proposed Solana route would therefore need clear contract information, supported custody and a documented operational path. None of those implementation questions is answered merely by the speed with which the underlying chain can confirm a transaction.

Anchorpoint’s current FAQ says Beta Access is live through selected authorized distributors for non-retail users, with HKDAP available on Ethereum during that stage. Full Launch is targeted as early as the end of 2026, subject to readiness across issuance, distribution and supporting infrastructure.

That sequencing matters because a technical integration and a customer rollout can progress on different schedules. An issuer may test issuance, while a distributor is still preparing onboarding or a wallet provider is checking how to display the asset.

Retail expansion also brings a different support burden. Institutions can negotiate workflows and coordinate directly with counterparties. A broader user base needs understandable transaction status, fees, recovery procedures and reliable routes for reporting a problem.

The meaningful milestone would be a named, operational service showing how a user obtains HKDAP, transacts with it and exits back into usable bank money when needed. A complete journey is more informative than the number of potential wallet integrations.

Liquidity matters throughout that journey. A payment network may operate continuously while currency conversion or redemption capacity is constrained at certain times. Users care about the completed payment, including its total cost, rather than only the blockchain leg.

Anchorpoint’s plan is therefore best understood as an attempt to place regulated Hong Kong dollar money closer to applications that might need it. The collaboration creates a route to wider distribution. Actual issuance, access conditions and repeated customer use will show how much of that opportunity becomes a functioning market.

#5179. Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin halts transfers after $40M drained in ‘security incident’

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Mercado Bitcoin suspended deposits and withdrawals after identifying a security incident in one of its systems on November 2. The Brazilian crypto exchange later published destination wallet addresses to help trace assets connected to the incident.

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company froze over 4.5 million USDT connected to the case. It is amongst other security incidents concerning crypto services, including Binance and old BTCPay Server software users, in the last few days.

Arkham separately valued wallets it attributed to the attacker at approximately $46 million on November 2. The tracked portfolio also included about $5.03 million in USDT, $3.02 million in USDC, $1.78 million in PEPE, $1.63 million in AAVE, and $1.46 million in PAX Gold.

Mercado Bitcoin responded quickly after discovering the breach; they claim it occurred overnight and that customers were financially unaffected while no data was lost.

They are investigating, tracking, and coordinating with the relevant authorities; deposits and withdrawals were stopped.

Following this, in a separate address, Mercado Bitcoin issued details of the addresses used on other blockchains for its transfers, including Bitcoin, Solana, Stellar, Tron, and their Ethereum-based/compatible services. It claimed the addresses were being published purely for tracing purposes.

The exchange also said it was working to restore operations safely and would keep customers informed through official channels. But there was no update about the reopening time or total financial impact.

Ardoino disclosed Tether’s intervention while sharing Mercado Bitcoin’s initial announcement.

“Tether froze more than 4.5M USDT related to this security incident,” he wrote.

Tether can block transfers of its tokens at specific addresses, helping restrict their movement during an investigation. This was the second time in the last seven days that Tether has frozen funds associated with exploits. The latest was with Binance, when over $6 billion was exploited.

Ardoino’s announcement left the next steps for those frozen tokens unspecified, including their possible return to Mercado Bitcoin.

The incident follows Binance’s disclosure that attackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from its wallets on October 29. Binance began reopening withdrawals on November 1 and committed to covering the losses.

BTCPay Server issued an advisory of their own on November 2 after receiving reports that Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from wallets that stored the spending keys on impacted servers.

They found web servers from version 2.4.1 or less were targeted, and the bad actors were also able to exploit a vulnerability that they patched in August through another method.

BTCPay recommends moving to fresh servers and moving existing wallet/seed to the new one, since updating the affected software might leave an open door for hackers.

The team added that wallets with their spending keys held outside the servers, like most hardware wallets, were unaffected by these thefts. It continues investigating the scope of the incident fully.

Brazilian crypto platform Mercado Bitcoin has confirmed the detection and containment of an issue in one of its systems. As a precaution, the exchange has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals, assuring clients of the safety of their assets and the absence of a data leak.

The incident occurred shortly after the platform passed a local licensing deadline.

According to independent blockchain company Hypernative, suspicious outflows from wallets linked to the exchange exceeded $40 million (approximately 217 million reais). Analysts recorded the movement of assets on the Ethereum, Bitcoin, Solana, Tron and Stellar (XLM) networks.

In total, the activity spanned at least 10 blockchains, also including Polygon, Arbitrum, Avalanche and BNB Smart Chain. The first suspicious transfers were recorded at around 02:15 UTC and involved Bitcoin deposit addresses attributed to the exchange.

Among the flagged assets were 106 BTC and 2,852 ETH. The hackers carried out direct token transfers, which indicates a compromise of operational reserves rather than segregated client assets.

Among the withdrawn assets, blockchain analysts recorded a large volume of Stellar tokens: about 6.7 million XLM were consolidated at addresses linked to the suspicious transactions.

As part of the investigation and coordination of efforts with the authorities, Mercado Bitcoin published a specific Stellar destination address to help the community and security firms track the movement of assets in real time.

The move is aimed at monitoring the movement of tokens and preventing their laundering through third-party services.

At the moment, the exchange is conducting an investigation, tracking the assets and promising to provide regular updates. The exchange has not yet confirmed the amount involved, disclosed which system was compromised or given a date for resuming deposits and withdrawals.

Until the platform fully resumes normal operations and the security of its infrastructure is confirmed, users are advised to refrain from making new deposits.

#5176. Base Sets November 5 Denim Activation as Apps Prepare for Native 200ms Blocks

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Base has put a specific time on its next network upgrade: November 5 at 18:00 UTC. The network’s status notice says mainnet is expected to remain operational through the Denim maintenance window and tells node operators to install the required release before activation.

For applications, the headline change is a shift to native blocks every 200 milliseconds. That is more than a quicker progress indicator: software that reads blocks, receipts and timestamps has to understand what the new cadence means.

Base’s Denim documentation describes a move from one canonical block every two seconds to five complete blocks each second, replacing Flashblocks. Applications following the earlier stream need to migrate to canonical block and RPC streams.

The distinction matters because applications build assumptions around the data they receive. A block identifier can be used to organize receipts, update a balance or decide when to refresh a trading screen. Increasing the frequency changes how often these processes run even if the underlying business action remains the same.

For an exchange, that can mean more updates to process between two user interactions. For an indexer, it means more block records and more frequent state changes. The challenge is keeping the application responsive without turning a faster chain into a backlog inside its own infrastructure.

Users often encounter several forms of confirmation that look similar in an interface. An application can display a submitted transaction, show that it has entered a block and later treat the result as sufficiently settled for its own purpose. Those are separate decisions.

A shorter block interval may improve the time to observe execution. It does not, on its own, establish how every bridge, exchange or financial application should handle finality. Those services have additional rules governing when a result can be relied on or a balance released.

The practical test is therefore end-to-end. A wallet that receives a faster network update but waits on a slow backend may show little improvement. A trading application that makes correct use of the new stream could offer a more immediate experience without claiming that all settlement risks have disappeared.

Denim also introduces millisecond-aware time information while preserving existing seconds-based fields. That creates a compatibility issue for systems whose logic assumes that a new block always brings a new whole-second timestamp.

Suppose an application groups events solely by the timestamp it has always stored. Multiple blocks can fall into the same second. If the application mistakes that shared value for a unique ordering key, it could merge unrelated records or process them in the wrong order.

This is an application-design example, not a report of an existing Base defect. It illustrates why support for a faster network requires more than changing a displayed number. Storage schemas, ordering rules and monitoring should all reflect the data actually provided.

Operators need to follow the official release requirements, while product teams need to check the assumptions in their own integrations. The node notice and application documentation answer different parts of that preparation.

The strongest evidence after activation will be stable block production, correctly indexed activity and normal handling of deposits, withdrawals and contract interactions. Those outcomes matter more to users than a theoretical throughput comparison.

Denim is scheduled infrastructure work, not an event that has already occurred. If the activation proceeds as planned, Base applications will have a different foundation for presenting transaction progress. Whether users notice a smoother service will depend on how well the surrounding software keeps pace with it.

The access to clean water isn’t taken for granted in many jurisdictions across the globe. Water. Org is here to fix it.

Ripple and Water.org are expanding a collaboration that has already helped more than one million people gain access to safe water or sanitation financing across Latin America.

The nonprofit, co-founded by Gary White and Matt Damon, is now layering Ripple Payments, the RLUSD stablecoin, and digital asset custody tools into its operations so capital can move faster and cheaper into emerging markets.

Water.org has used Ripple Payments to move more than $3.2 million across four markets.

Settlement times in Mexico and Brazil dropped from two to three days to same-day, while payment processing became available around the clock instead of being limited by a single daily banking cutoff.

Transaction fees fell by as much as 66 percent, so a larger share of every dollar reaches borrowers rather than intermediaries.

Ripple committed $6 million over three years to support Water.org programs such as WaterCredit, which partners with local financial institutions to offer affordable loans for household taps, toilets, and piped connections.

Finance as a tool to solve the water crisis 💧@Water co-founders Matt Damon and Gary White joined @bgarlinghouse on the Swell main stage to share how Ripple Payments and RLUSD are helping @Water reach more people, faster. pic.twitter.com/VXdttesBK6

Separately, Water.org received a $1.25 million grant in Ripple’s RLUSD through the Stablecoin Impact Fund. That capital is intended to expand stablecoin-enabled WaterCredit disbursements into Indonesia, the Philippines, and Uganda.

Water.org will also begin using Ripple’s Wallet-as-a-Service technology to manage digital assets as the programs scale. Beyond the direct funding, Ripple joined Get Blue, the Water.org movement modeled after the (RED) campaign, as its exclusive digital-asset and fintech partner.

Founding brand partners include Gap, Amazon, Starbucks, and Ecolab. Ripple’s first year of Get Blue support helped reach 400,000 people, with the three-year commitment expected to support 1.2 million as Water.org works toward its broader goal of reaching 200 million people by 2030.

Gary White, co-founder and CEO of Water.org, said the actual water crisis is fundamentally a funding-flow problem rather than a lack of capital, and that Ripple’s infrastructure has shown what efficient movement of money looks like in practice.

Brad Garlinghouse, Ripple’s CEO, noted that the partnership demonstrates the original promise of crypto and blockchain: making money move faster, more efficiently, and globally for real-world needs.

White and Matt Damon joined Garlinghouse for a fireside chat at Ripple Swell in New York.

The expanded setup combines traditional philanthropic capital with on-chain settlement and custody so that repaid loans can be recycled into new lending through vehicles such as the WaterEquity Everspring Fund.

For Water.org, the practical result is more of each donated or invested dollar reaching families that need household water connections. For Ripple, it is another demonstration of its payments and stablecoin stack operating outside pure trading venues and inside humanitarian finance.
